verses.after: One who speaks faithfully tells what is right; a false witness tells deceit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever speaks truth declares what is right, but a false witness speaks deceit.

verses.before: There is one whose reckless speech is like the thrusts of a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
verses.after: Reckless speech stabs like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is one whose reckless speech is like the thrusts of a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

verses.before: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue only for a moment.
verses.after: Truthful lips endure forever; a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue only for a moment.

verses.rationale: Keep counselors of peace rather than generic peacemakers.
verses.before: Deceit is in the heart of people who devise evil, but people who counsel peace have joy.
verses.after: Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil; joy belongs to those who counsel peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deceit is in the heart of those who devise evil, but those who counsel peace have joy.

verses.rationale: Preserve proverb’s absolute form; genre note handles scope.
verses.before: No harm overtakes the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.
verses.after: No harm befalls the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: No harm overtakes the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.

verses.rationale: Keep words contrasted with faithful action.
verses.before: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but people who act faithfully are the LORD’s delight.
verses.after: Lying lips are detestable to the LORD; those who act faithfully delight him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who act faithfully are the LORD’s delight.

verses.rationale: Retain discretion without equating concealment with lying.
verses.before: A prudent person conceals knowledge, but the heart of fools proclaims folly.
verses.after: A prudent person keeps knowledge to himself; the heart of fools proclaims folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: A prudent person conceals knowledge, but the heart of fools proclaims folly.

verses.before: The hand of the diligent will rule, but the slack hand will be put to forced labor.
verses.after: Diligent hands will rule, but slack hands will face forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hand of the diligent will rule, but the slack hand will be put to forced labor.

verses.before: Anxiety in a person’s heart weighs it down, but a good word makes it glad.
verses.after: Anxiety weighs down a person’s heart, but a good word makes it glad.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anxiety in a person’s heart weighs it down, but a good word makes it glad.

verses.rationale: Choose guidance sense of difficult verb; note alternative.
verses.before: The righteous guide their neighbor carefully, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
verses.after: The righteous give guidance to their neighbors, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous guide their neighbor carefully, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.

verses.rationale: Keep difficult hunting image; specify interpretive choice in note.
verses.before: A lazy person does not roast what they have hunted, but diligence is a precious possession.
verses.after: The lazy do not roast their game, but diligence is a person’s precious possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: A lazy person does not roast what they have hunted, but diligence is a precious possession.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned no death without emending to death.
verses.before: In the path of righteousness is life, and along its pathway there is no death.
verses.after: On the path of righteousness is life; along its trail there is no death.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the path of righteousness is life, and along its pathway there is no death.

verses.rationale: Supply accepts from elliptical first line.
verses.before: A wise child receives a father’s discipline, but a scoffer does not listen to rebuke.
verses.after: A wise son accepts his father’s discipline; a scoffer does not listen to rebuke.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wise child receives a father’s discipline, but a scoffer does not listen to rebuke.

verses.before: From the fruit of the mouth a person eats what is good, but the appetite of the treacherous is for violence.
verses.after: From the fruit of his mouth a person eats good things, but the appetite of the faithless is for violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the fruit of the mouth a person eats what is good, but the appetite of the treacherous is for violence.

verses.rationale: Keep guarding contrast and wide opening.
verses.before: Whoever guards their mouth guards their life, but whoever opens their lips wide comes to ruin.
verses.after: Whoever guards his mouth protects his life; whoever opens his lips wide invites ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever guards their mouth guards their life, but whoever opens their lips wide comes to ruin.

verses.before: The appetite of the lazy person desires and has nothing, but the appetite of the diligent is richly satisfied.
verses.after: The sluggard craves and has nothing; the diligent are richly satisfied.
verses.tsw_comparator: The appetite of the lazy person desires and has nothing, but the appetite of the diligent is richly satisfied.

verses.before: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
verses.after: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring a stench and shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.

verses.before: Righteousness guards the one whose way has integrity, but wickedness overturns the sinner.
verses.after: Righteousness guards those whose way is blameless; wickedness overturns the sinner.
verses.tsw_comparator: Righteousness guards the one whose way has integrity, but wickedness overturns the sinner.

verses.before: One pretends to be rich yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor yet has great wealth.
verses.after: One person pretends to be rich and has nothing; another pretends to be poor and owns great wealth.
verses.tsw_comparator: One pretends to be rich yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor yet has great wealth.

verses.before: The ransom of a person’s life may be their wealth, but the poor hear no threat.
verses.after: A person’s wealth can ransom his life, but the poor hear no threat.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ransom of a person’s life may be their wealth, but the poor hear no threat.

verses.rationale: Preserve rejoicing light and extinguished lamp.
verses.before: The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
verses.after: The light of the righteous shines joyfully, but the lamp of the wicked goes out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

verses.before: Pride produces only conflict, but wisdom is with those who receive counsel.
verses.after: Pride produces only quarrels, but wisdom is with those who take counsel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pride produces only conflict, but wisdom is with those who receive counsel.

verses.rationale: Retain hevel ambiguity rather than assert fraud only.
verses.before: Wealth gained too quickly diminishes, but whoever gathers little by little makes it increase.
verses.after: Wealth gained from emptiness dwindles, but whoever gathers little by little increases it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wealth gained too quickly diminishes, but whoever gathers little by little makes it increase.

verses.before: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
verses.after: Hope long delayed makes the heart sick; a desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.

verses.rationale: Preserve liability rather than supply physical destruction.
verses.before: Whoever despises a word brings destruction upon themselves, but whoever fears the commandment will be rewarded.
verses.after: Whoever despises a word will be held liable for it; whoever respects a command will be repaid.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever despises a word brings destruction upon themselves, but whoever fears the commandment will be rewarded.

verses.before: The instruction of the wise is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.
verses.after: The instruction of the wise is a fountain of life, turning people away from death’s snares.
verses.tsw_comparator: The instruction of the wise is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.

verses.before: Good insight brings favor, but the way of the treacherous is hard.
verses.after: Good judgment wins favor, but the way of the faithless is hard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Good insight brings favor, but the way of the treacherous is hard.

verses.before: Everyone prudent acts with knowledge, but a fool displays folly.
verses.after: Every prudent person acts with knowledge; a fool spreads his folly abroad.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone prudent acts with knowledge, but a fool displays folly.

verses.rationale: Follow falls rather than emend causes.
verses.before: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
verses.after: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

verses.before: Poverty and disgrace come to the one who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction will be honored.
verses.after: Poverty and dishonor come to one who rejects discipline; whoever keeps correction will be honored.
verses.tsw_comparator: Poverty and disgrace come to the one who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction will be honored.

verses.rationale: Keep contrast without forcing one explanatory link.
verses.before: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is an abomination to fools.
verses.after: A desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.
verses.tsw_comparator: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is an abomination to fools.

verses.rationale: Follow both read forms as declarative.
verses.before: Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but a companion of fools will suffer harm.
verses.after: Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise; a companion of fools suffers harm.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but a companion of fools will suffer harm.

verses.before: Trouble pursues sinners, but good repays the righteous.
verses.after: Trouble pursues sinners, but good repays the righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: Trouble pursues sinners, but good repays the righteous.

verses.rationale: Keep two generations and transferred wealth.
verses.before: A good person leaves an inheritance to children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored up for the righteous.
verses.after: A good person leaves an inheritance to grandchildren, but a sinner’s wealth is stored up for the righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: A good person leaves an inheritance to children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored up for the righteous.

verses.rationale: Preserve structural injustice rather than blame poverty on sloth.
verses.before: The field of the poor may produce abundant food, but it can be swept away through injustice.
verses.after: The unplowed field of the poor has abundant food, but it is swept away by injustice.
verses.tsw_comparator: The field of the poor may produce abundant food, but it can be swept away through injustice.

verses.rationale: Retain rod and severe love/hate claim; do not sanitize corporal punishment.
verses.before: Whoever withholds the rod hates their child, but whoever loves their child is diligent in discipline.
verses.after: Whoever holds back his rod hates his son; whoever loves him is diligent in discipline.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever withholds the rod hates their child, but whoever loves their child is diligent in discipline.

verses.before: The righteous eat until their appetite is satisfied, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.
verses.after: The righteous eat until satisfied, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous eat until their appetite is satisfied, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.

verses.before: A wise woman builds her house, but Folly tears it down with her own hands.
verses.after: A wise woman builds her house, but Folly tears it down with her own hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wise woman builds her house, but Folly tears it down with her own hands.

verses.rationale: Retain conduct as expression of reverence.
verses.before: Whoever walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but one whose ways are crooked despises the LORD.
verses.after: Whoever walks uprightly fears the LORD; whoever twists his ways despises him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but one whose ways are crooked despises the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep difficult rod image without inventing its target.
verses.before: In the mouth of a fool is a rod for pride, but the lips of the wise will guard them.
verses.after: In a fool’s mouth is a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise protect them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the mouth of a fool is a rod for pride, but the lips of the wise will guard them.

verses.rationale: Choose empty rather than hygienically clean.
verses.before: Where there are no oxen, the manger is clean, but abundant produce comes through the strength of an ox.
verses.after: Where there are no oxen, the feeding trough is empty, but an ox’s strength brings a plentiful harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Where there are no oxen, the manger is clean, but abundant produce comes through the strength of an ox.

verses.before: A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
verses.after: A faithful witness does not lie; a false witness breathes out lies.
verses.tsw_comparator: A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.

verses.before: A scoffer seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
verses.after: A scoffer seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes readily to the discerning.
verses.tsw_comparator: A scoffer seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.

verses.before: Leave the presence of a fool, for there you will not find lips of knowledge.
verses.after: Leave the presence of a fool; you will not find knowledgeable speech there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Leave the presence of a fool, for there you will not find lips of knowledge.

verses.before: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand their way, but the folly of fools is deception.
verses.after: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand their way; the folly of fools is deceit.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand their way, but the folly of fools is deception.

verses.rationale: Select mock guilt reading; note guilt offering ambiguity.
verses.before: Fools mock at guilt, but among the upright there is favor.
verses.after: Fools mock at guilt, but among the upright there is goodwill.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fools mock at guilt, but among the upright there is favor.

verses.rationale: Preserve inward experience and outsider limitation.
verses.before: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares fully in its joy.
verses.after: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no outsider can share its joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares fully in its joy.

verses.before: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
verses.after: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.

verses.before: There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the way of death.
verses.after: There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the ways of death.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the way of death.

verses.rationale: Keep coexistence rather than equate all joy with sorrow.
verses.before: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy may be grief.
verses.after: Even in laughter the heart can ache, and joy can end in sorrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy may be grief.

verses.rationale: Supply deeds implied by parallel ways; retain moral return.
verses.before: The one who turns away in heart will be filled with the fruit of their ways, but a good person with the fruit of their deeds.
verses.after: The wayward in heart have their fill of their own ways; a good person has his fill from his own deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who turns away in heart will be filled with the fruit of their ways, but a good person with the fruit of their deeds.

verses.before: The simple believe every word, but the prudent consider their steps.
verses.after: The inexperienced believe every word; the prudent consider their steps.
verses.tsw_comparator: The simple believe every word, but the prudent consider their steps.

verses.before: The wise fear and turn away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
verses.after: The wise fear and turn away from evil; a fool rages on in confidence.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wise fear and turn away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.

verses.rationale: Preserve anger and plotting as distinct.
verses.before: One who is quick-tempered acts foolishly, and one who devises evil is hated.
verses.after: A quick-tempered person acts foolishly; a schemer is hated.
verses.tsw_comparator: One who is quick-tempered acts foolishly, and one who devises evil is hated.

verses.before: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
verses.after: The inexperienced inherit folly; the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

verses.before: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
verses.after: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

verses.rationale: Retain harsh social observation, not endorsement.
verses.before: The poor are disliked even by their neighbor, but the rich have many friends.
verses.after: The poor are hated even by their neighbors, but the rich have many who love them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The poor are disliked even by their neighbor, but the rich have many friends.

verses.before: Whoever despises a neighbor sins, but blessed is the one who shows favor to the poor.
verses.after: Whoever despises his neighbor sins; happy is the one who shows mercy to the lowly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever despises a neighbor sins, but blessed is the one who shows favor to the poor.

verses.rationale: Keep planning contrast and covenant-like virtue pair.
verses.before: Do not people who devise evil go astray? But steadfast love and faithfulness belong to people who devise good.
verses.after: Do not those who plot evil go astray? Faithful love and faithfulness meet those who plan good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not those who devise evil go astray? But steadfast love and faithfulness belong to those who devise good.

verses.before: In all labor there is profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
verses.after: All hard work brings some gain; mere talk leads only to need.
verses.tsw_comparator: In all labor there is profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.

verses.rationale: Keep wealth without emendation and emphatic repetition.
verses.before: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the folly of fools remains folly.
verses.after: The crown of the wise is their wealth; the folly of fools is still folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the folly of fools remains folly.

verses.before: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who breathes out lies deceives.
verses.after: A truthful witness rescues lives, but one who breathes out lies is deceitful.
verses.tsw_comparator: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who breathes out lies deceives.

verses.rationale: Keep ambiguous his rather than settle ownership silently.
verses.before: In the fear of the LORD there is strong confidence, and there will be refuge for one’s children.
verses.after: In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence, and his children will have a refuge.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fear of the LORD there is strong confidence, and there will be refuge for one’s children.

verses.before: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.
verses.after: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning people away from death’s snares.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.

verses.before: In a multitude of people is a king’s glory, but without people a ruler is ruined.
verses.after: A large population is a king’s splendor; without a people, a ruler is ruined.
verses.tsw_comparator: In a multitude of people is a king’s glory, but without people a ruler is ruined.

verses.before: Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding, but one who is quick-tempered exalts folly.
verses.after: One slow to anger has great understanding; a short temper raises folly high.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding, but one who is quick-tempered exalts folly.

verses.before: A tranquil heart gives life to the body, but jealousy rots the bones.
verses.after: A tranquil heart gives life to the body, but jealousy rots the bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: A tranquil heart gives life to the body, but jealousy rots the bones.

verses.before: Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever honors God shows favor to the needy.
verses.after: Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker; whoever shows mercy to the needy honors him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever honors God shows favor to the needy.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned death rather than integrity variant.
verses.before: The wicked are overthrown by their own evil, but the righteous find refuge even in death.
verses.after: The wicked are brought down by their evil, but the righteous find refuge even in death.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked are overthrown by their own evil, but the righteous find refuge even in death.

verses.before: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, but what is among fools becomes known.
verses.after: Wisdom rests in a discerning heart; even among fools she makes herself known.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, but what is among fools becomes known.

verses.rationale: Read rare disgrace sense without importing faithful love.
verses.before: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
verses.after: Righteousness raises a nation up, but sin is a disgrace to peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.

verses.before: A king’s favor is toward a servant who acts wisely, but wrath falls upon one who brings shame.
verses.after: A king favors a servant who acts wisely, but his fury falls on one who brings shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: A king’s favor is toward a servant who acts wisely, but wrath falls upon one who brings shame.

verses.before: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
verses.after: A gentle answer turns back fury; a hurtful word stirs up anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

verses.rationale: Choose attractive use of knowledge; keep gushing.
verses.before: The tongue of the wise makes knowledge good, but the mouth of fools pours out folly.
verses.after: The tongue of the wise makes knowledge welcome; the mouth of fools gushes folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The tongue of the wise makes knowledge good, but the mouth of fools pours out folly.

verses.before: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, watching the evil and the good.
verses.after: The LORD’s eyes are everywhere, watching the evil and the good.
verses.tsw_comparator: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, watching the evil and the good.

verses.before: A healing tongue is a tree of life, but perversity in it breaks the spirit.
verses.after: A healing tongue is a tree of life; a crooked tongue breaks the spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: A healing tongue is a tree of life, but perversity in it breaks the spirit.

verses.before: A fool despises a father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
verses.after: A fool despises his father’s discipline; whoever keeps correction becomes prudent.
verses.tsw_comparator: A fool despises a father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.

verses.rationale: Keep wealth rather than abstract virtue.
verses.before: In the house of the righteous there is great treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.
verses.after: The house of the righteous holds great wealth; the income of the wicked brings trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the house of the righteous there is great treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.

verses.rationale: Retain scattered knowledge and asymmetrical heart.
verses.before: The lips of the wise scatter knowledge, but the hearts of fools do not.
verses.after: The lips of the wise scatter knowledge; the heart of fools does not.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lips of the wise scatter knowledge, but the hearts of fools do not.

verses.rationale: Keep ritual/ethical contrast without rejecting sacrifice itself.
verses.before: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is the LORD’s delight.
verses.after: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright delights him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is the LORD’s delight.

verses.before: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the LORD loves the one who pursues righteousness.
verses.after: The way of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but he loves those who pursue righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the LORD loves the one who pursues righteousness.

verses.before: Severe discipline awaits the one who abandons the path; whoever hates correction will die.
verses.after: Harsh discipline awaits one who leaves the path; whoever hates correction will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: Severe discipline awaits the one who abandons the path; whoever hates correction will die.

verses.rationale: Retain two underworld terms and inference.
verses.before: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD; how much more the hearts of human beings!
verses.after: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD— how much more human hearts!
verses.tsw_comparator: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD; how much more the hearts of human beings!

verses.before: A scoffer does not love the one who corrects them; they will not go to the wise.
verses.after: A scoffer does not love being corrected; he will not go to the wise.
verses.tsw_comparator: A scoffer does not love the one who corrects them; they will not go to the wise.

verses.before: A joyful heart makes the face glad, but sorrow of heart crushes the spirit.
verses.after: A joyful heart brightens the face; a sorrowful heart crushes the spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: A joyful heart makes the face glad, but sorrow of heart crushes the spirit.

verses.rationale: Follow mouth read form, not written face.
verses.before: The heart of the discerning seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools feeds on folly.
verses.after: A discerning heart seeks knowledge; the mouth of fools feeds on folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the discerning seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools feeds on folly.

verses.rationale: Keep affliction without reducing it to attitude.
verses.before: All the days of the afflicted are difficult, but a good heart has a continual feast.
verses.after: All the days of the afflicted are hard, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the days of the afflicted are difficult, but a good heart has a continual feast.

verses.before: Better is a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
verses.after: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.

verses.before: Better is a meal of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
verses.after: Better a meal of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is a meal of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.

verses.before: A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but one slow to anger calms a quarrel.
verses.after: A furious man stirs up conflict; one slow to anger quiets a quarrel.
verses.tsw_comparator: A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but one slow to anger calms a quarrel.

verses.before: The way of the lazy is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a level road.
verses.after: A sluggard’s way is like a hedge of thorns; the path of the upright is a raised highway.
verses.tsw_comparator: The way of the lazy is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a level road.

verses.rationale: Retain gender and mother’s distinct treatment.
verses.before: A wise child makes a father glad, but a foolish person despises their mother.
verses.after: A wise son brings his father joy; a foolish man despises his mother.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wise child makes a father glad, but a foolish person despises their mother.

verses.before: Folly is joy to one lacking sense, but a person of understanding walks straight ahead.
verses.after: Folly is joy to one who lacks sense; a person of understanding walks straight.
verses.tsw_comparator: Folly is joy to one lacking sense, but a person of understanding walks straight ahead.

verses.before: Plans fail where there is no counsel, but with many advisers they are established.
verses.after: Plans fail without consultation; with many counselors they stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Plans fail where there is no counsel, but with many advisers they are established.

verses.before: A person has joy in an appropriate answer, and a word at the right time— how good it is!
verses.after: A fitting answer brings a person joy; how good is a word at the right time!
verses.tsw_comparator: A person has joy in an appropriate answer, and a word at the right time— how good it is!

verses.rationale: Preserve vertical image without naming heaven.
verses.before: The path of life leads upward for the prudent, turning them away from Sheol below.
verses.after: For the discerning, the path of life leads upward, away from Sheol below.
verses.tsw_comparator: The path of life leads upward for the prudent, turning them away from Sheol below.

verses.before: The LORD tears down the house of the proud but establishes the boundary of the widow.
verses.after: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but secures the widow’s boundary.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD tears down the house of the proud but establishes the boundary of the widow.

verses.rationale: Retain ritual purity language for speech.
verses.before: Evil plans are an abomination to the LORD, but gracious words are pure.
verses.after: Evil plans are detestable to the LORD, but pleasant words are pure.
verses.tsw_comparator: Evil plans are an abomination to the LORD, but gracious words are pure.

verses.rationale: Keep corrupt gain and household consequences.
verses.before: Whoever is greedy for unjust gain troubles their own household, but whoever hates bribes will live.
verses.after: Whoever is greedy for gain troubles his household; whoever hates bribes will live.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever is greedy for unjust gain troubles their own household, but whoever hates bribes will live.

verses.before: The heart of the righteous considers how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil.
verses.after: The heart of the righteous weighs an answer; the mouth of the wicked gushes evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the righteous considers how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil.

verses.before: The LORD is far from the wicked, but hears the prayer of the righteous.
verses.after: The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is far from the wicked, but hears the prayer of the righteous.

verses.before: The light of the eyes makes the heart glad, and good news strengthens the bones.
verses.after: Bright eyes bring joy to the heart; good news nourishes the bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: The light of the eyes makes the heart glad, and good news strengthens the bones.

verses.rationale: Retain listening ear as person metonym.
verses.before: The ear that listens to life-giving correction will dwell among the wise.
verses.after: An ear that listens to life-giving correction will dwell among the wise.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ear that listens to life-giving correction will dwell among the wise.

verses.rationale: Keep self-harm and gained heart idiom.
verses.before: Whoever rejects discipline despises their own life, but whoever listens to correction gains understanding.
verses.after: Whoever rejects discipline despises his own life; whoever listens to correction gains understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever rejects discipline despises their own life, but whoever listens to correction gains understanding.

verses.before: The fear of the LORD is instruction in wisdom, and before honor comes humility.
verses.after: The fear of the LORD teaches wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fear of the LORD is instruction in wisdom, and before honor comes humility.

verses.rationale: Keep human planning and divine answer distinct.
verses.before: The plans of the heart belong to a person, but the answer of the tongue comes from the LORD.
verses.after: The arrangements of the heart belong to a person, but the tongue’s answer comes from the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The plans of the heart belong to a person, but the answer of the tongue comes from the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve spirits rather than flatten to deeds.
verses.before: All a person’s ways are pure in their own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirits.
verses.after: All a person’s ways seem pure in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs spirits.
verses.tsw_comparator: All a person’s ways are pure in their own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirits.

verses.rationale: Retain concrete entrusting metaphor; explain selectively.
verses.before: Commit your works to the LORD, and your plans will be established.
verses.after: Roll your works onto the LORD, and your plans will be established.
verses.tsw_comparator: Commit your works to the LORD, and your plans will be established.

verses.rationale: Preserve difficult divine-purpose claim without doctrinal expansion.
verses.before: The LORD has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for a day of trouble.
verses.after: The LORD has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for a day of disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for a day of trouble.

verses.before: Everyone proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD; be assured, they will not go unpunished.
verses.after: Every proud heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured, it will not go unpunished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD; be assured, they will not go unpunished.

verses.before: Through steadfast love and faithfulness guilt is covered, and through the fear of the LORD one turns away from evil.
verses.after: Through faithful love and faithfulness guilt is atoned for; through the fear of the LORD one turns from evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through steadfast love and faithfulness guilt is covered, and through the fear of the LORD one turns away from evil.

verses.before: When a person’s ways please the LORD, even their enemies are made to be at peace with them.
verses.after: When a person’s ways please the LORD, he makes even his enemies be at peace with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When a person’s ways please the LORD, even their enemies are made to be at peace with them.

verses.before: Better is a little with righteousness than abundant income without justice.
verses.after: Better a little with righteousness than abundant income without justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is a little with righteousness than abundant income without justice.

verses.before: A person’s heart plans their way, but the LORD establishes their steps.
verses.after: A human heart plans its way, but the LORD establishes its steps.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person’s heart plans their way, but the LORD establishes their steps.

verses.rationale: Render royal judicial obligation, not historical infallibility claim.
verses.before: An oracle is on the lips of a king; in judgment his mouth must not betray justice.
verses.after: An oracle is on the lips of a king; his mouth must not betray justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: An oracle is on the lips of a king; in judgment his mouth must not betray justice.

verses.rationale: Keep commercial instruments and stone weights.
verses.before: Honest balances and scales belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are the LORD’s concern.
verses.after: Honest balances and scales belong to the LORD; all the weights in the pouch are his work.
verses.tsw_comparator: Honest balances and scales belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are the LORD’s concern.

verses.rationale: Retain royal ideal and throne foundation.
verses.before: Doing wickedness is an abomination to kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.
verses.after: Wicked action is detestable to kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Doing wickedness is an abomination to kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.

verses.before: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, and the king loves one who speaks what is upright.
verses.after: Righteous lips delight kings; they love one who speaks uprightly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, and the king loves one who speaks what is upright.

verses.rationale: Keep lethal power and pacifying wisdom.
verses.before: A king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise person will appease it.
verses.after: A king’s fury sends messengers of death, but a wise person appeases it.
verses.tsw_comparator: A king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise person will appease it.

verses.before: In the light of a king’s face there is life, and the king’s favor is like a cloud of spring rain.
verses.after: In the light of a king’s face is life; his favor is like a cloud of spring rain.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the light of a king’s face there is life, and the king’s favor is like a cloud of spring rain.

verses.before: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To acquire understanding is preferable to silver.
verses.after: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To acquire understanding is more desirable than silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To acquire understanding is preferable to silver.

verses.before: The highway of the upright turns away from evil; whoever guards their way protects their life.
verses.after: The highway of the upright turns away from evil; whoever guards his way protects his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The highway of the upright turns away from evil; whoever guards their way protects their life.

verses.before: Pride comes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
verses.after: Pride comes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pride comes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

verses.rationale: Follow humble read form; keep spoils.
verses.before: Better to be lowly in spirit with the poor than to divide plunder with the proud.
verses.after: Better a lowly spirit among the humble than a share of plunder with the proud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better to be lowly in spirit with the poor than to divide plunder with the proud.

verses.before: Whoever pays attention to a matter will find good, and blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD.
verses.after: Whoever attends to a matter wisely finds good; happy is the one who trusts in the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever pays attention to a matter will find good, and blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain sweet speech and learning/persuasion sense.
verses.before: The wise in heart are called discerning, and sweetness of speech increases persuasiveness.
verses.after: The wise in heart are called discerning; sweetness of speech adds persuasive power.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wise in heart are called discerning, and sweetness of speech increases persuasiveness.

verses.rationale: Keep difficult discipline clause without explanatory insertion.
verses.before: Understanding is a fountain of life to the one who possesses it, but the discipline of fools is folly.
verses.after: Good judgment is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Understanding is a fountain of life to the one who possesses it, but the discipline of fools is folly.

verses.before: The heart of the wise makes their mouth discerning and adds persuasiveness to their lips.
verses.after: A wise heart gives insight to its mouth and adds persuasive power to its lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the wise makes their mouth discerning and adds persuasiveness to their lips.

verses.before: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the body.
verses.after: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the body.

verses.before: There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the way of death.
verses.after: There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the ways of death.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a way that seems right to a person, but its end is the way of death.

verses.before: A worker’s appetite works for them, for their mouth urges them onward.
verses.after: A worker’s appetite works for him; his mouth drives him on.
verses.tsw_comparator: A worker’s appetite works for them, for their mouth urges them onward.

verses.before: A worthless person digs up evil, and their speech is like scorching fire.
verses.after: A worthless man digs up evil; on his lip is a scorching fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: A worthless person digs up evil, and their speech is like scorching fire.

verses.rationale: Keep covert speech and relational damage.
verses.before: A perverse person sows conflict, and a gossip separates close friends.
verses.after: A twisted man stirs up conflict; a whisperer separates close friends.
verses.tsw_comparator: A perverse person sows conflict, and a gossip separates close friends.

verses.rationale: Retain violence and euphemistic not good.
verses.before: A violent person entices a neighbor and leads them into a way that is not good.
verses.after: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him on a way that is not good.
verses.tsw_comparator: A violent person entices a neighbor and leads them into a way that is not good.

verses.before: One who closes their eyes is planning perversity; one who purses the lips brings evil to pass.
verses.after: One who narrows his eyes plans perversity; one who presses his lips together brings evil to completion.
verses.tsw_comparator: One who closes their eyes is planning perversity; one who purses the lips brings evil to pass.

verses.rationale: Keep gray hair and moral path.
verses.before: Gray hair is a crown of glory when it is found in the way of righteousness.
verses.after: Gray hair is a beautiful crown; it is found on the way of righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gray hair is a crown of glory when it is found in the way of righteousness.

verses.rationale: Retain strength comparison without erasing warfare.
verses.before: One slow to anger is better than a warrior, and one who rules their spirit than one who captures a city.
verses.after: Better one slow to anger than a warrior, one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city.
verses.tsw_comparator: One slow to anger is better than a warrior, and one who rules their spirit than one who captures a city.

verses.rationale: Keep ancient lot practice and divine attribution.
verses.before: The lot is cast into the lap, but every decision from it is from the LORD.
verses.after: The lot is cast into the lap, but every decision it gives comes from the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lot is cast into the lap, but every decision from it is from the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain sacrificial meals, not generic abundance only.
verses.before: Better is a dry morsel with quiet than a house full of feasting with conflict.
verses.after: Better a dry crust with quiet than a house full of sacrificial feasts with quarrels.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is a dry morsel with quiet than a house full of feasting with conflict.

verses.before: A servant who acts wisely will rule over a child who brings shame and will share an inheritance among the family.
verses.after: A servant who acts wisely will rule over a shameful son and share the inheritance among the brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: A servant who acts wisely will rule over a child who brings shame and will share an inheritance among the family.

verses.before: The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests hearts.
verses.after: A crucible is for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD tests hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests hearts.

verses.before: An evildoer listens to wicked lips, and a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue.
verses.after: An evildoer listens to wicked lips; a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue.
verses.tsw_comparator: An evildoer listens to wicked lips, and a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue.

verses.before: Whoever mocks the poor insults their Maker, and whoever rejoices at disaster will not go unpunished.
verses.after: Whoever mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever rejoices at disaster will not go unpunished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever mocks the poor insults their Maker, and whoever rejoices at disaster will not go unpunished.

verses.rationale: Retain fathers rather than general parents.
verses.before: Children’s children are the crown of the aged, and parents are the glory of their children.
verses.after: Grandchildren are the crown of the old, and fathers are the glory of their children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Children’s children are the crown of the aged, and parents are the glory of their children.

verses.rationale: Keep ascending comparison and social rank.
verses.before: Fine speech does not suit a fool, much less lying lips a noble person.
verses.after: Fine speech does not suit a fool; how much less do lying lips suit a noble!
verses.tsw_comparator: Fine speech does not suit a fool, much less lying lips a noble person.

verses.rationale: Retain viewpoint qualifier; description not endorsement.
verses.before: A gift is like a precious stone in the eyes of its owner; wherever it turns, it seems to prosper.
verses.after: A bribe is a precious stone in its owner’s eyes; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: A gift is like a precious stone in the eyes of its owner; wherever it turns, it seems to prosper.

verses.before: Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.
verses.after: Whoever covers an offense seeks love; whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.

verses.rationale: Preserve exact hundred and physical blows.
verses.before: A rebuke goes deeper into a discerning person than a hundred blows into a fool.
verses.after: A rebuke sinks deeper into one who understands than a hundred blows into a fool.
verses.tsw_comparator: A rebuke goes deeper into a discerning person than a hundred blows into a fool.

verses.rationale: Keep ambiguous messenger without angel insertion.
verses.before: An evil person seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger will be sent against them.
verses.after: An evil person seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
verses.tsw_comparator: An evil person seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger will be sent against them.

verses.before: Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool among folly.
verses.after: Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in the midst of folly.

verses.rationale: Follow depart read form and repeated evil.
verses.before: Whoever returns evil for good, evil will not depart from their house.
verses.after: Whoever repays good with evil— evil will not leave his house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever returns evil for good, evil will not depart from their house.

verses.before: The beginning of conflict is like releasing water; so leave a quarrel before it breaks out.
verses.after: Starting a quarrel is like letting water loose; leave the dispute before it breaks out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The beginning of conflict is like releasing water; so leave a quarrel before it breaks out.

verses.before: Whoever declares the wicked righteous and whoever condemns the righteous— both are an abomination to the LORD.
verses.after: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent— both are detestable to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever declares the wicked righteous and whoever condemns the righteous— both are an abomination to the LORD.

verses.before: Why should a fool have money in hand to buy wisdom when there is no heart to understand?
verses.after: Why is there a price in a fool’s hand to buy wisdom when he has no sense?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should a fool have money in hand to buy wisdom when there is no heart to understand?

verses.before: A friend loves at all times, and a brother or sister is born for adversity.
verses.after: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: A friend loves at all times, and a brother or sister is born for adversity.

verses.rationale: Retain before neighbor rather than force for neighbor.
verses.before: One lacking sense strikes hands and becomes surety before a neighbor.
verses.after: A person without sense clasps hands in a pledge, guaranteeing a debt in his neighbor’s presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: One lacking sense strikes hands and becomes surety before a neighbor.

verses.before: Whoever loves transgression loves conflict; whoever makes their doorway high seeks destruction.
verses.after: Whoever loves quarrels loves wrongdoing; whoever raises his doorway high seeks destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever loves transgression loves conflict; whoever makes their doorway high seeks destruction.

verses.before: One with a crooked heart finds no good, and one with a twisted tongue falls into trouble.
verses.after: A twisted heart finds no good; a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: One with a crooked heart finds no good, and one with a twisted tongue falls into trouble.

verses.before: The one who fathers a fool has sorrow, and the parent of a senseless child has no joy.
verses.after: The one who fathers a fool has sorrow; a fool’s father has no joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who fathers a fool has sorrow, and the parent of a senseless child has no joy.

verses.before: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries the bones.
verses.after: A joyful heart brings good healing; a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries the bones.

verses.rationale: Render from bosom as concealed; keep bent paths.
verses.before: The wicked take a bribe in secret to bend the paths of justice.
verses.after: A wicked person takes a concealed bribe to bend the paths of justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked take a bribe in secret to bend the paths of justice.

verses.before: Wisdom is before the face of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool are at the ends of the earth.
verses.after: Wisdom is before the face of the discerning, but a fool’s eyes roam to the ends of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wisdom is before the face of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool are at the ends of the earth.

verses.before: A foolish child is grief to a father and bitterness to the one who gave birth.
verses.after: A foolish son is grief to his father and bitterness to the woman who bore him.
verses.tsw_comparator: A foolish child is grief to a father and bitterness to the one who gave birth.

verses.before: It is not good to punish the righteous, or to strike honorable people for their uprightness.
verses.after: It is not good to fine the innocent or to strike nobles for doing right.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is not good to punish the righteous, or to strike honorable people for their uprightness.

verses.rationale: Follow precious/noble read form; note cool written form.
verses.before: One who restrains words has knowledge, and one of understanding has a calm spirit.
verses.after: One who knows restrains his words; a person of understanding has a noble spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: One who restrains words has knowledge, and one of understanding has a calm spirit.

verses.before: Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise; when they close their lips, they are considered discerning.
verses.after: Even a fool is considered wise when silent, discerning when he closes his lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise; when they close their lips, they are considered discerning.

verses.rationale: Preserve antisocial defiance, not solitude generally.
verses.before: One who isolates themselves seeks their own desire and breaks out against all sound wisdom.
verses.after: One who isolates himself pursues his own desire and breaks out against all sound wisdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: One who isolates themselves seeks their own desire and breaks out against all sound wisdom.

verses.before: A fool takes no delight in understanding, but only in revealing their own heart.
verses.after: A fool takes no pleasure in understanding, only in exposing what is in his heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: A fool takes no delight in understanding, but only in revealing their own heart.

verses.before: When wickedness comes, contempt also comes, and with dishonor comes disgrace.
verses.after: When wickedness comes, contempt comes too; with dishonor comes disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: When wickedness comes, contempt also comes, and with dishonor comes disgrace.

verses.rationale: Preserve two water images without forcing contrast.
verses.before: The words of a person’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a flowing stream.
verses.after: The words of a person’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a flowing stream.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of a person’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a flowing stream.

verses.before: It is not good to show favor to the wicked or to deprive the righteous of justice.
verses.after: It is not good to favor the guilty and turn aside the innocent in judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is not good to show favor to the wicked or to deprive the righteous of justice.

verses.before: A fool’s lips enter into conflict, and their mouth invites a beating.
verses.after: A fool’s lips enter quarrels; his mouth calls for blows.
verses.tsw_comparator: A fool’s lips enter into conflict, and their mouth invites a beating.

verses.before: A fool’s mouth is their destruction, and their lips are a snare for their life.
verses.after: A fool’s mouth is his ruin; his lips are a snare for his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: A fool’s mouth is their destruction, and their lips are a snare for their life.

verses.before: The words of a gossip are like delicious morsels; they go down to the innermost parts.
verses.after: A whisperer’s words are like tasty morsels; they go down into the innermost belly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of a gossip are like delicious morsels; they go down to the innermost parts.

verses.before: Whoever is slack in their work is a sibling to one who destroys.
verses.after: One who is slack in his work is brother to a destroyer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever is slack in their work is a sibling to one who destroys.

verses.before: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are secure.
verses.after: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are safe on high.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are secure.

verses.before: The wealth of the rich is their strong city and like a high wall in their imagination.
verses.after: The wealth of the rich is their fortified city, like a high wall in their imagination.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wealth of the rich is their strong city and like a high wall in their imagination.

verses.before: Before destruction a person’s heart is proud, but before honor comes humility.
verses.after: Before destruction a person’s heart grows proud; before honor comes humility.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before destruction a person’s heart is proud, but before honor comes humility.

verses.before: Whoever answers before hearing shows folly and shame.
verses.after: Answering before listening is folly and dishonor for the speaker.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever answers before hearing shows folly and shame.

verses.rationale: Retain question and two senses of spirit’s condition.
verses.before: A person’s spirit can endure sickness, but a crushed spirit— who can bear it?
verses.after: A person’s spirit can sustain him in illness, but who can bear a crushed spirit?
verses.tsw_comparator: A person’s spirit can endure sickness, but a crushed spirit— who can bear it?

verses.rationale: Keep repeated knowledge and body parts.
verses.before: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
verses.after: A discerning heart acquires knowledge; the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.

verses.rationale: Retain gift rather than automatically bribe.
verses.before: A person’s gift makes room for them and brings them before the great.
verses.after: A person’s gift makes room for him and brings him before the great.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person’s gift makes room for them and brings them before the great.

verses.rationale: Follow conjunction read form and forensic testing.
verses.before: The first to state a case seems right until another comes and examines them.
verses.after: The first to present his case seems right, until his neighbor comes and examines him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first to state a case seems right until another comes and examines them.

verses.rationale: Keep lot procedure and powerful parties.
verses.before: The lot brings disputes to an end and decides between powerful opponents.
verses.after: Casting lots ends disputes and separates powerful opponents.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lot brings disputes to an end and decides between powerful opponents.

verses.rationale: Supply harder to win for compressed comparison; keep bars.
verses.before: A brother or sister offended is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a fortress.
verses.after: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city; quarrels are like the bars of a palace.
verses.tsw_comparator: A brother or sister offended is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a fortress.

verses.before: From the fruit of a person’s mouth their stomach is satisfied; they are filled with the produce of their lips.
verses.after: A person’s belly is filled by the fruit of his mouth; he is filled by the produce of his lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the fruit of a person’s mouth their stomach is satisfied; they are filled with the produce of their lips.

verses.rationale: Keep ambiguous it and consequences of speech.
verses.before: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and people who love it will eat its fruit.
verses.after: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.

verses.rationale: Retain wife without added adjective good.
verses.before: Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
verses.after: Whoever finds a wife finds good and obtains favor from the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.

verses.before: The poor speak with pleas, but the rich answer harshly.
verses.after: The poor speak with pleading, but the rich answer harshly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The poor speak with pleas, but the rich answer harshly.

verses.rationale: Choose ruin sense of difficult verb; preserve close friendship.
verses.before: A person with many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a sibling.
verses.after: A person with many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who clings more closely than a brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person with many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a sibling.

verses.rationale: Do not insert rich into second line.
verses.before: Better is a poor person who walks in integrity than one crooked in speech and a fool.
verses.after: Better a poor person who walks with integrity than a fool with twisted lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is a poor person who walks in integrity than one crooked in speech and a fool.

verses.rationale: Keep appetite/desire and sinful missing image.
verses.before: Desire without knowledge is not good, and whoever hurries with their feet misses the way.
verses.after: Desire without knowledge is not good; hasty feet miss the way.
verses.tsw_comparator: Desire without knowledge is not good, and whoever hurries with their feet misses the way.

verses.before: A person’s folly ruins their way, and then their heart rages against the LORD.
verses.after: A person’s folly wrecks his way, then his heart rages against the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person’s folly ruins their way, and then their heart rages against the LORD.

verses.before: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor are separated even from a friend.
verses.after: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor are separated from their neighbor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor are separated even from a friend.

verses.before: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who breathes out lies will not escape.
verses.after: A false witness will not go unpunished; one who breathes out lies will not escape.
verses.tsw_comparator: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who breathes out lies will not escape.

verses.before: Many seek the favor of a generous person, and everyone is a friend to one who gives gifts.
verses.after: Many seek the favor of a generous noble; everyone is a friend to a giver of gifts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many seek the favor of a generous person, and everyone is a friend to one who gives gifts.

verses.rationale: Follow written negative in difficult final clause; explicitly note read-form alternative.
verses.before: All the relatives of the poor may hate them; how much more do their friends avoid them. They pursue them with words, but they are gone.
verses.after: All a poor man’s brothers hate him; how much more do his friends keep their distance! He pursues words, but they are not there.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the relatives of the poor may hate them; how much more do their friends avoid them. They pursue them with words, but they are gone.

verses.before: Whoever acquires understanding loves their own life; whoever guards discernment will find good.
verses.after: Whoever acquires understanding loves his own life; whoever guards insight will find good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever acquires understanding loves their own life; whoever guards discernment will find good.

verses.rationale: Preserve difference from verse 5 final verb.
verses.before: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who breathes out lies will perish.
verses.after: A false witness will not go unpunished; one who breathes out lies will perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who breathes out lies will perish.

verses.rationale: Keep ancient social hierarchy without modern substitution.
verses.before: Luxury is not fitting for a fool, much less a servant ruling over princes.
verses.after: Luxury does not suit a fool; how much less does ruling princes suit a servant!
verses.tsw_comparator: Luxury is not fitting for a fool, much less a servant ruling over princes.

verses.before: A person’s discretion makes them slow to anger, and it is their glory to overlook an offense.
verses.after: Good judgment makes a person slow to anger; it is his glory to overlook an offense.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person’s discretion makes them slow to anger, and it is their glory to overlook an offense.

verses.before: A king’s anger is like the roaring of a lion, but the king’s favor is like dew upon the grass.
verses.after: A king’s rage is like a young lion’s roar; his favor is like dew on grass.
verses.tsw_comparator: A king’s anger is like the roaring of a lion, but the king’s favor is like dew upon the grass.

verses.before: A foolish child is disaster to a father, and the quarrels of a spouse are a continual dripping.
verses.after: A foolish son is his father’s ruin; a wife’s quarrels are a constant dripping.
verses.tsw_comparator: A foolish child is disaster to a father, and the quarrels of a spouse are a continual dripping.

verses.before: House and wealth are inherited from parents, but a prudent spouse is from the LORD.
verses.after: A house and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife comes from the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: House and wealth are inherited from parents, but a prudent spouse is from the LORD.

verses.before: Laziness casts one into deep sleep, and an idle person will go hungry.
verses.after: Laziness sinks a person into deep sleep; a slack person will go hungry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Laziness casts one into deep sleep, and an idle person will go hungry.

verses.rationale: Follow die read form, not be executed written form.
verses.before: Whoever keeps the commandment keeps their life; whoever despises their ways will die.
verses.after: Whoever keeps a command protects his life; whoever despises his ways will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever keeps the commandment keeps their life; whoever despises their ways will die.

verses.before: Whoever shows favor to the poor lends to the LORD, and the LORD will repay the deed.
verses.after: Whoever shows mercy to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will repay that deed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever shows favor to the poor lends to the LORD, and the LORD will repay the deed.

verses.rationale: Preserve warning against death without softening first imperative.
verses.before: Discipline your child while there is hope; do not set your heart on their destruction.
verses.after: Discipline your son while there is hope; do not set your heart on his death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Discipline your child while there is hope; do not set your heart on their destruction.

verses.rationale: Follow great anger read form and repeated rescue.
verses.before: One of great anger must bear the penalty; if you rescue them, you will only have to do it again.
verses.after: A hot-tempered person bears the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do it again.
verses.tsw_comparator: One of great anger must bear the penalty; if you rescue them, you will only have to do it again.

verses.before: Listen to counsel and receive discipline so that you may become wise in your future.
verses.after: Listen to counsel and receive discipline, so that you may be wise in your later days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to counsel and receive discipline so that you may become wise in your future.

verses.rationale: Keep many human plans versus enduring counsel.
verses.before: Many are the plans in a person’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will stand.
verses.after: Many are the plans in a person’s heart, but the LORD’s counsel will stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many are the plans in a person’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will stand.

verses.rationale: Choose desired quality sense and preserve abrupt comparison.
verses.before: What is desirable in a person is steadfast love, and a poor person is better than a liar.
verses.after: What is desired in a person is faithful love; better to be poor than a liar.
verses.tsw_comparator: What is desirable in a person is steadfast love, and a poor person is better than a liar.

verses.before: The fear of the LORD leads to life; one rests satisfied and is not visited by harm.
verses.after: The fear of the LORD leads to life; one rests satisfied, untouched by harm.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fear of the LORD leads to life; one rests satisfied and is not visited by harm.

verses.before: A lazy person buries a hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to the mouth.
verses.after: A sluggard buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: A lazy person buries a hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to the mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserve different recipients of lesson and real blows.
verses.before: Strike a scoffer, and the simple may become prudent; correct the discerning, and they will understand knowledge.
verses.after: Strike a scoffer, and the inexperienced learn prudence; correct a discerning person, and he understands knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: Strike a scoffer, and the simple may become prudent; correct the discerning, and they will understand knowledge.

verses.before: Whoever mistreats a father and drives away a mother is a child who brings shame and disgrace.
verses.after: One who robs his father and drives away his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever mistreats a father and drives away a mother is a child who brings shame and disgrace.

verses.rationale: Read ironic conditional warning; note compressed syntax.
verses.before: My child, if you stop listening to discipline, you will stray from words of knowledge.
verses.after: Stop listening to discipline, my son, and you will wander from words of knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: My child, if you stop listening to discipline, you will stray from words of knowledge.

verses.before: A worthless witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked devours wrongdoing.
verses.after: A worthless witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: A worthless witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked devours wrongdoing.

verses.before: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, and blows for the backs of fools.
verses.after: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, and blows for the backs of fools.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, and blows for the backs of fools.

verses.before: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
verses.after: Wine is a scoffer; strong drink is a brawler. Whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; whoever is led astray by them is not wise.

verses.before: The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion; whoever provokes him endangers their own life.
verses.after: A king’s terror is like a young lion’s roar; whoever provokes him endangers his own life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion; whoever provokes him endangers their own life.

verses.before: It is an honor for a person to stay out of conflict, but every fool bursts into quarrels.
verses.after: It is an honor to stay out of a quarrel, but every fool rushes into one.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is an honor for a person to stay out of conflict, but every fool bursts into quarrels.

verses.rationale: Follow read-form continuation and seasonal sequence.
verses.before: The lazy do not plow in the proper season; at harvest they will look and find nothing.
verses.after: A sluggard will not plow in the cold season; at harvest he looks for a crop, but there is none.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lazy do not plow in the proper season; at harvest they will look and find nothing.

verses.before: Counsel in the human heart is deep water, but a person of understanding will draw it out.
verses.after: Counsel in a person’s heart is deep water, but someone with understanding draws it out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Counsel in the human heart is deep water, but a person of understanding will draw it out.

verses.before: Many people proclaim their own steadfast love, but a faithful person— who can find?
verses.after: Many proclaim their own faithful love, but who can find a trustworthy person?
verses.tsw_comparator: Many people proclaim their own steadfast love, but a faithful person— who can find?

verses.before: The righteous walk in their integrity; blessed are their children after them.
verses.after: The righteous walk with integrity; happy are their children after them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous walk in their integrity; blessed are their children after them.

verses.rationale: Retain winnowing image and judicial gaze.
verses.before: A king sitting on the judgment throne winnows all evil with his eyes.
verses.after: A king sitting on the judgment throne winnows out all evil with his eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: A king sitting on the judgment throne winnows all evil with his eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserve rhetorical question and self-purification claim.
verses.before: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure; I am clean from my sin”?
verses.after: Who can say, “I have made my heart clean; I am pure from my sin”?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure; I am clean from my sin”?

verses.before: Unequal weights and unequal measures— both alike are an abomination to the LORD.
verses.after: Two different weights, two different measures— both are detestable to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Unequal weights and unequal measures— both alike are an abomination to the LORD.

verses.before: Even a child makes themselves known by their deeds, whether their conduct is pure and upright.
verses.after: Even a youth is known by his actions, whether his conduct is pure and upright.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even a child makes themselves known by their deeds, whether their conduct is pure and upright.

verses.before: The hearing ear and the seeing eye— the LORD has made both of them.
verses.after: The hearing ear and the seeing eye— the LORD made them both.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hearing ear and the seeing eye— the LORD has made both of them.

verses.before: Do not love sleep, or you will become poor; open your eyes, and you will have enough bread.
verses.after: Do not love sleep, or you will become poor; open your eyes, and you will have enough bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not love sleep, or you will become poor; open your eyes, and you will have enough bread.

verses.before: “Bad, bad,” says the buyer, but after going away the buyer boasts.
verses.after: “Bad, bad!” says the buyer; then he goes away and boasts.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Bad, bad,” says the buyer, but after going away the buyer boasts.

verses.before: There is gold and an abundance of jewels, but lips of knowledge are a precious treasure.
verses.after: There is gold, and jewels in abundance, but knowledgeable lips are a precious treasure.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is gold and an abundance of jewels, but lips of knowledge are a precious treasure.

verses.rationale: Follow feminine read form, note written plural strangers.
verses.before: Take the garment of one who becomes surety for a stranger; hold it as security for an outsider.
verses.after: Take the garment of one who guarantees a stranger’s debt; hold it as a pledge when he guarantees an outsider woman’s debt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take the garment of one who becomes surety for a stranger; hold it as security for an outsider.

verses.before: Bread gained by deception is sweet to a person, but afterward the mouth is filled with gravel.
verses.after: Bread gained by deceit tastes sweet, but afterward the mouth is filled with gravel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bread gained by deception is sweet to a person, but afterward the mouth is filled with gravel.

verses.before: Plans are established through counsel; conduct war with wise guidance.
verses.after: Plans are established through counsel; wage war with sound guidance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Plans are established through counsel; conduct war with wise guidance.

verses.before: A gossip reveals secrets; so do not associate with one who opens their lips carelessly.
verses.after: A gossip goes about revealing confidences; do not associate with one whose lips are always open.
verses.tsw_comparator: A gossip reveals secrets; therefore do not associate with one who opens their lips carelessly.

verses.before: Whoever curses father or mother, their lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.
verses.after: Whoever curses his father or mother— his lamp will go out in deepest darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever curses father or mother, their lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.

verses.before: An inheritance gained hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.
verses.after: An inheritance hastily seized at the beginning will not be blessed at the end.
verses.tsw_comparator: An inheritance gained hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.

verses.before: Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Wait for the LORD, who will save you.
verses.after: Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Wait for the LORD, and he will deliver you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Wait for the LORD, who will save you.

verses.before: Unequal weights are an abomination to the LORD, and dishonest scales are not good.
