verses.after: Two different weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are not good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Unequal weights are an abomination to the LORD, and dishonest scales are not good.

verses.before: A person’s steps are from the LORD; how then can anyone fully understand their own way?
verses.after: A man’s steps come from the LORD; how, then, can a human understand his own way?
verses.tsw_comparator: A person’s steps are from the LORD; how then can anyone fully understand their own way?

verses.before: It is a trap to say rashly, “Holy!” and only afterward consider the vow.
verses.after: It is a snare to blurt out, “This is holy!” and only afterward consider the vows.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is a trap to say rashly, “Holy!” and only afterward consider the vow.

verses.before: A wise king winnows the wicked and turns the wheel over them.
verses.after: A wise king winnows the wicked and drives a threshing wheel over them.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wise king winnows the wicked and turns the wheel over them.

verses.rationale: Retain breath rather than impose a technical soul doctrine.
verses.before: The human spirit is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the innermost parts.
verses.after: The human breath is the LORD’s lamp, searching every chamber within.
verses.tsw_comparator: The human spirit is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the innermost parts.

verses.before: Steadfast love and faithfulness preserve a king, and the throne is supported by steadfast love.
verses.after: Faithful love and faithfulness guard a king; through faithful love he sustains his throne.
verses.tsw_comparator: Steadfast love and faithfulness preserve a king, and the throne is supported by steadfast love.

verses.before: The glory of the young is their strength, and the splendor of the old is gray hair.
verses.after: The glory of young men is their strength; the splendor of the old is gray hair.
verses.tsw_comparator: The glory of the young is their strength, and the splendor of the old is gray hair.

verses.rationale: Follow cleansing read form; preserve physical harm.
verses.before: Blows that wound cleanse away evil, and strokes reach the innermost parts.
verses.after: Wounding blows scour away evil; stripes cleanse the chambers within.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blows that wound cleanse away evil, and strokes reach the innermost parts.

verses.before: A king’s heart is like channels of water in the hand of the LORD; the LORD turns it wherever desired.
verses.after: A king’s heart is like channels of water in the LORD’s hand; he turns it wherever he wishes.
verses.tsw_comparator: A king’s heart is like channels of water in the hand of the LORD; the LORD turns it wherever desired.

verses.before: Every way of a person is right in their own eyes, but the LORD weighs hearts.
verses.after: Every way seems right in a person’s own eyes, but the LORD weighs hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every way of a person is right in their own eyes, but the LORD weighs hearts.

verses.before: To practice righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
verses.after: Doing righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: To practice righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.

verses.rationale: Choose lamp sense; note plowed-field alternative.
verses.before: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— the lamp of the wicked— are sin.
verses.after: Haughty eyes and a swollen heart— the lamp of the wicked—are sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— the lamp of the wicked— are sin.

verses.before: The plans of the diligent surely lead to abundance, but everyone who hurries comes only to poverty.
verses.after: The plans of the diligent lead only to gain; everyone who hurries comes only to need.
verses.tsw_comparator: The plans of the diligent surely lead to abundance, but everyone who hurries comes only to poverty.

verses.rationale: Follow death-seekers text, not death-snares alternative.
verses.before: Gaining treasure with a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor, a snare of death.
verses.after: Treasures gained by a lying tongue are a vanishing breath for those seeking death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gaining treasure with a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor, a snare of death.

verses.before: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to practice justice.
verses.after: The violence of the wicked drags them away, because they refuse to do justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to practice justice.

verses.before: The way of the guilty is crooked, but the work of the pure is upright.
verses.after: The way of the guilty is twisted, but the conduct of the pure is straight.
verses.tsw_comparator: The way of the guilty is crooked, but the work of the pure is upright.

verses.before: Better to live on a corner of a roof than share a house with a quarrelsome spouse.
verses.after: Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better to live on a corner of a roof than share a house with a quarrelsome spouse.

verses.before: The appetite of the wicked desires evil; their neighbor receives no mercy from them.
verses.after: The wicked crave evil; their neighbor finds no mercy in their eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The appetite of the wicked desires evil; their neighbor receives no mercy from them.

verses.rationale: Preserve indirect and direct learning contrast.
verses.before: When a scoffer is punished, the simple become wise; when the wise are instructed, they gain knowledge.
verses.after: When a scoffer is punished, the inexperienced become wise; when the wise receive instruction, they gain knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: When a scoffer is punished, the simple become wise; when the wise are instructed, they gain knowledge.

verses.rationale: Choose divine referent; flag righteous person alternative.
verses.before: The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked and overturns the wicked into ruin.
verses.after: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked; he overturns the wicked into disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked and overturns the wicked into ruin.

verses.before: Whoever closes their ear to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered.
verses.after: Whoever shuts his ear to the poor person’s cry will also cry out and receive no answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever closes their ear to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered.

verses.rationale: Keep gift and bribe distinct, descriptive claim.
verses.before: A gift given secretly calms anger, and a concealed present strong wrath.
verses.after: A gift in secret quiets anger; a concealed bribe quiets fierce rage.
verses.tsw_comparator: A gift given secretly calms anger, and a concealed present strong wrath.

verses.before: The practice of justice is joy to the righteous but terror to people who do evil.
verses.after: Doing justice brings joy to the righteous but terror to those who do wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: The practice of justice is joy to the righteous but terror to those who do evil.

verses.before: A person who wanders from the way of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.
verses.after: One who wanders from the way of understanding will rest among the assembly of the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person who wanders from the way of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.

verses.before: Whoever loves pleasure will become poor; whoever loves wine and oil will not become rich.
verses.after: Whoever loves pleasure will become needy; whoever loves wine and oil will not grow rich.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever loves pleasure will become poor; whoever loves wine and oil will not become rich.

verses.before: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous in place of the upright.
verses.after: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless take the place of the upright.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous in place of the upright.

verses.before: Better to live in a wilderness than with a quarrelsome and angry spouse.
verses.after: Better to live in a wilderness than with a quarrelsome and angry wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better to live in a wilderness than with a quarrelsome and angry spouse.

verses.before: Precious treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish person swallows them up.
verses.after: Precious treasure and oil are in the wise person’s home, but a fool swallows them up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Precious treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish person swallows them up.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated righteousness rather than replace with prosperity.
verses.before: Whoever pursues righteousness and steadfast love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
verses.after: Whoever pursues righteousness and faithful love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever pursues righteousness and steadfast love finds life, righteousness, and honor.

verses.before: A wise person can scale a city of warriors and bring down the stronghold they trusted.
verses.after: A wise person scales a city of warriors and brings down the stronghold they trust.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wise person can scale a city of warriors and bring down the stronghold they trusted.

verses.rationale: Preserve paired organs and guarding repetition.
verses.before: Whoever guards mouth and tongue guards their life from troubles.
verses.after: Whoever guards his mouth and tongue guards his life from troubles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever guards mouth and tongue guards their life from troubles.

verses.before: “Scoffer” is the name of the proud and arrogant person who acts with excessive pride.
verses.after: Proud and arrogant—Scoffer is his name; he acts with overflowing pride.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Scoffer” is the name of the proud and arrogant person who acts with excessive pride.

verses.rationale: Retain desire and hands as agents.
verses.before: The desire of the lazy kills them, because their hands refuse to work.
verses.after: A sluggard’s craving kills him, for his hands refuse to work.
verses.tsw_comparator: The desire of the lazy kills them, because their hands refuse to work.

verses.rationale: Connect sluggard subject; keep intense repetition.
verses.before: All day long they crave more and more, but the righteous give and do not hold back.
verses.after: All day long he craves and craves, but the righteous give without holding back.
verses.tsw_comparator: All day long they crave more and more, but the righteous give and do not hold back.

verses.before: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination— how much more when brought with evil intent!
verses.after: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable; how much more when brought with an evil purpose!
verses.tsw_comparator: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination— how much more when brought with evil intent!

verses.rationale: Keep difficult enduring speech without over-resolving.
verses.before: A false witness will perish, but one who listens carefully will speak enduringly.
verses.after: A lying witness will perish, but a person who listens will speak enduringly.
verses.tsw_comparator: A false witness will perish, but one who listens carefully will speak enduringly.

verses.rationale: Follow considers and singular way read forms.
verses.before: A wicked person hardens their face, but the upright consider their way.
verses.after: A wicked man puts on a bold face, but the upright considers his way.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wicked person hardens their face, but the upright consider their way.

verses.before: There is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel that can stand against the LORD.
verses.after: There is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel that can stand against the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel that can stand against the LORD.

verses.before: The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory belongs to the LORD.
verses.after: The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but deliverance belongs to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory belongs to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Supply good from favorable name context.
verses.before: A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, and favor rather than silver and gold.
verses.after: A good name is more desirable than great wealth; favor is better than silver and gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, and favor rather than silver and gold.

verses.before: Rich and poor meet together; the LORD is the Maker of them all.
verses.after: Rich and poor meet together; the LORD is the Maker of them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rich and poor meet together; the LORD is the Maker of them all.

verses.before: The prudent see danger and hide themselves, but the simple pass on and suffer for it.
verses.after: The prudent see danger and hide, but the inexperienced go on and suffer for it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prudent see danger and hide themselves, but the simple pass on and suffer for it.

verses.rationale: Keep compressed relation of humility and fear; note alternative.
verses.before: The reward of humility and the fear of the LORD is riches, honor, and life.
verses.after: The reward of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The reward of humility and the fear of the LORD is riches, honor, and life.

verses.before: Thorns and snares are in the way of the crooked; whoever guards their life stays far from them.
verses.after: Thorns and snares lie on the crooked person’s way; whoever guards his life stays far from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thorns and snares are in the way of the crooked; whoever guards their life stays far from them.

verses.rationale: Preserve ambiguous his way instead of supplying should.
verses.before: Train a child according to the way they should go; even when old, they will not depart from it.
verses.after: Train a youth according to his way; even when old, he will not turn from it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Train a child according to the way they should go; even when old, they will not depart from it.

verses.before: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
verses.after: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is a servant to the lender.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

verses.rationale: Follow reap read form and preserve rod.
verses.before: Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of their fury will fail.
verses.after: Whoever sows injustice reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will fail.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of their fury will fail.

verses.rationale: Render good eye idiom through generosity.
verses.before: One with a generous eye will be blessed, for they share their bread with the poor.
verses.after: The generous will be blessed, for they share their bread with the poor.
verses.tsw_comparator: One with a generous eye will be blessed, for they share their bread with the poor.

verses.before: Drive out the scoffer, and conflict will go out; quarreling and disgrace will cease.
verses.after: Drive out a scoffer, and conflict leaves; disputes and dishonor cease.
verses.tsw_comparator: Drive out the scoffer, and conflict will go out; quarreling and disgrace will cease.

verses.rationale: Follow pure read form and retain royal friendship.
verses.before: Whoever loves purity of heart and has gracious speech, the king will be their friend.
verses.after: Whoever loves purity of heart and speaks graciously will have the king as a friend.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever loves purity of heart and has gracious speech, the king will be their friend.

verses.before: The eyes of the LORD guard knowledge, but the LORD overturns the words of the treacherous.
verses.after: The LORD’s eyes guard knowledge, but he overturns the words of the faithless.
verses.tsw_comparator: The eyes of the LORD guard knowledge, but the LORD overturns the words of the treacherous.

verses.before: The lazy person says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the street!”
verses.after: A sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the public square!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The lazy person says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the street!”

verses.rationale: Preserve divine anger and plural women.
verses.before: The mouth of forbidden relationships is a deep pit; one under the LORD’s indignation falls into it.
verses.after: The mouth of forbidden women is a deep pit; one under the LORD’s anger falls into it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The mouth of forbidden relationships is a deep pit; one under the LORD’s indignation falls into it.

verses.rationale: Retain rod rather than abstract correction only.
verses.before: Folly is bound to the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far away.
verses.after: Folly is bound to a youth’s heart; the rod of discipline drives it far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Folly is bound to the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far away.

verses.rationale: Choose parallel harmful practices; note compressed pronoun ambiguity.
verses.before: Whoever oppresses the poor to increase their own wealth, or gives to the rich, comes only to poverty.
verses.after: Oppressing the poor to increase one’s wealth and giving to the rich lead only to need.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever oppresses the poor to increase their own wealth, or gives to the rich, comes only to poverty.

verses.before: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge.
verses.after: Turn your ear and hear the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge.

verses.rationale: Preserve inward retention and spoken readiness.
verses.before: For it will be pleasant if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready upon your lips.
verses.after: It is pleasant when you keep them within you, when they are all ready on your lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it will be pleasant if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready upon your lips.

verses.before: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I teach them to you today— yes, to you.
verses.after: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I make them known to you today—to you yourself.
verses.tsw_comparator: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I teach them to you today— yes, to you.

verses.rationale: Follow excellent/chief read-form interpretation; note thirty and formerly alternatives.
verses.before: Have I not written for you thirty sayings of counsel and knowledge,
verses.after: Have I not written excellent sayings for you, with counsel and knowledge,
verses.tsw_comparator: Have I not written for you thirty sayings of counsel and knowledge,

verses.before: to make you know the certainty of truthful words, so that you may return truthful words to people who sent you?
verses.after: to make you know the reliability of true words, so you can bring back truthful words to those who sent you?
verses.tsw_comparator: to make you know the certainty of truthful words, so that you may return truthful words to those who sent you?

verses.rationale: Keep exploitation of vulnerability and court gate.
verses.before: Do not rob the poor because they are poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,
verses.after: Do not rob the poor because they are poor; do not crush the afflicted at the gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not rob the poor because they are poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,

verses.rationale: Preserve judicial defense and lethal wordplay.
verses.before: for the LORD will plead their case and will take the life of people who take from them.
verses.after: For the LORD will plead their case and rob their robbers of life.
verses.tsw_comparator: for the LORD will plead their case and will take the life of those who take from them.

verses.before: Do not become a companion of an angry person, and do not go with one given to rage,
verses.after: Do not befriend a hot-tempered person or associate with a furious man,
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not become a companion of an angry person, and do not go with one given to rage,

verses.before: lest you learn their ways and take a snare upon your life.
verses.after: or you may learn his ways and take a snare for your own life.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest you learn their ways and take a snare upon your life.

verses.rationale: Keep physical pledge explained by second line.
verses.before: Do not be among those who strike hands in pledge, among people who become surety for debts.
verses.after: Do not be among those who clasp hands in a pledge, those who guarantee debts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be among those who strike hands in pledge, among those who become surety for debts.

verses.before: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
verses.after: If you have nothing to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
verses.tsw_comparator: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?

verses.before: Do not move the ancient boundary that your ancestors established.
verses.after: Do not move the ancient boundary marker that your ancestors set in place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not move the ancient boundary that your ancestors established.

verses.rationale: Retain rhetorical question and court service.
verses.before: Do you see someone skilled in their work? They will stand before kings; they will not stand before obscure people.
verses.after: Have you seen someone skilled at his work? He will stand before kings, not before obscure people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you see someone skilled in their work? They will stand before kings; they will not stand before obscure people.

verses.rationale: Keep attention to situation and food/person ambiguity.
verses.before: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what is before you,
verses.after: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what is before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what is before you,

verses.rationale: Retain alarming restraint image; explanatory note.
verses.before: and put a knife to your throat if you have a great appetite.
verses.after: Put a knife to your throat if you are ruled by appetite.
verses.tsw_comparator: and put a knife to your throat if you have a great appetite.

verses.before: Do not desire the ruler’s delicacies, for they are deceptive food.
verses.after: Do not crave his delicacies, for that food is deceptive.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not desire the ruler’s delicacies, for they are deceptive food.

verses.rationale: Choose understanding as basis for restraint.
verses.before: Do not exhaust yourself to become rich; have the understanding to stop.
verses.after: Do not wear yourself out getting rich; have the sense to stop.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not exhaust yourself to become rich; have the understanding to stop.

verses.rationale: Follow eye/flight read forms; keep disappearance.
verses.before: When your eyes fly toward wealth, it is gone, for it surely makes wings for itself and flies like an eagle toward heaven.
verses.after: Will you set your eyes on it? It is gone! Wealth surely makes itself wings and flies toward heaven like an eagle.
verses.tsw_comparator: When your eyes fly toward wealth, it is gone, for it surely makes wings for itself and flies like an eagle toward heaven.

verses.before: Do not eat the bread of one with a stingy eye, and do not desire their delicacies,
verses.after: Do not eat the bread of the stingy or crave their delicacies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not eat the bread of one with a stingy eye, and do not desire their delicacies,

verses.rationale: Retain inward reckoning, not general positive-thinking maxim.
verses.before: for as they calculate within themselves, so they are. “Eat and drink,” they say to you, but their heart is not with you.
verses.after: For he is like one calculating inwardly. “Eat and drink,” he tells you, but his heart is not with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: for as they calculate within themselves, so they are. “Eat and drink,” they say to you, but their heart is not with you.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily revulsion and wasted courtesy.
verses.before: You will vomit up the morsel you ate and waste your pleasant words.
verses.after: You will vomit the morsel you ate and waste your pleasant words.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will vomit up the morsel you ate and waste your pleasant words.

verses.before: Do not speak in the hearing of a fool, for they will despise the wisdom of your words.
verses.after: Do not speak in a fool’s hearing, for he will despise the good sense of your words.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not speak in the hearing of a fool, for they will despise the wisdom of your words.

verses.before: Do not move an ancient boundary or enter the fields of the fatherless,
verses.after: Do not move the ancient boundary marker or encroach on the fields of the fatherless.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not move an ancient boundary or enter the fields of the fatherless,

verses.before: for their Redeemer is strong; the Redeemer will plead their case against you.
verses.after: For their Redeemer is strong; he will plead their case against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: for their Redeemer is strong; the Redeemer will plead their case against you.

verses.before: Apply your heart to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.
verses.after: Bring your heart to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: Apply your heart to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.

verses.rationale: Preserve source’s bodily punishment claim without softening.
verses.before: Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you strike with the rod, the child will not die.
verses.after: Do not withhold discipline from a youth; if you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you strike with the rod, the child will not die.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated blow and underworld contrast.
verses.before: You may strike with the rod and rescue their life from Sheol.
verses.after: You will strike him with a rod and rescue his life from Sheol.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may strike with the rod and rescue their life from Sheol.

verses.before: My child, if your heart is wise, my own heart will rejoice.
verses.after: My son, if your heart becomes wise, my own heart will rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: My child, if your heart is wise, my own heart will rejoice.

verses.before: My innermost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is upright.
verses.after: My innermost being will exult when your lips speak what is right.
verses.tsw_comparator: My innermost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is upright.

verses.before: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but remain in the fear of the LORD all day long.
verses.after: Do not let your heart envy sinners; instead, fear the LORD all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but remain in the fear of the LORD all day long.

verses.before: Surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
verses.after: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.

verses.before: Hear, my child, and become wise; direct your heart in the way.
verses.after: Listen, my son, and become wise; lead your heart straight along the way.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, my child, and become wise; direct your heart in the way.

verses.rationale: Retain excessive consumption, not ban on food types.
verses.before: Do not be among people who drink too much wine, or among those who gorge themselves on meat,
verses.after: Do not join those who drink too much wine or those who gorge themselves on meat,
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be among those who drink too much wine, or among those who gorge themselves on meat,

verses.before: for the drunkard and glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe a person in rags.
verses.after: for the drunkard and the glutton become poor, and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
verses.tsw_comparator: for the drunkard and glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe a person in rags.

verses.rationale: Preserve aged mother’s claim to respect.
verses.before: Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
verses.after: Listen to your father who gave you life; do not despise your mother when she is old.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.

verses.rationale: Keep acquisition metaphor and three qualities.
verses.before: Buy truth and do not sell it— wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
verses.after: Buy truth, and do not sell it— wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Buy truth and do not sell it— wisdom, discipline, and understanding.

verses.rationale: Follow all four read forms, preserve fatherhood.
verses.before: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; the one who fathers a wise child will be glad.
verses.after: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; one who fathers a wise son will be glad in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; the one who fathers a wise child will be glad.

verses.rationale: Keep blessing-like wish and mother repeated.
verses.before: Let your father and mother be glad; let the one who gave birth to you rejoice.
verses.after: May your father and mother be glad; may the woman who bore you rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your father and mother be glad; let the one who gave birth to you rejoice.

verses.rationale: Follow keep/watch read form, not delight written form.
verses.before: My child, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.
verses.after: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes keep watch over my ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: My child, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.

verses.rationale: Keep two dangerous cavities and distinct terms.
verses.before: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman a narrow well.
verses.after: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and the forbidden woman a narrow well.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman a narrow well.

verses.rationale: Preserve ambush and multiplication of betrayal.
verses.before: She lies in wait like a robber and increases the treacherous among humanity.
verses.after: She too lies in wait like a robber and increases the faithless among humankind.
verses.tsw_comparator: She lies in wait like a robber and increases the treacherous among humanity.

verses.rationale: Retain six questions and physical effects.
verses.before: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has conflicts? Who has complaints? Who has wounds without cause? Who has reddened eyes?
verses.after: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has quarrels? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has conflicts? Who has complaints? Who has wounds without cause? Who has reddened eyes?

verses.rationale: Answer previous questions without inserting new referent.
verses.before: People who linger long over wine, people who go to search out mixed wine.
verses.after: Those who linger over wine, those who go seeking mixed drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who linger long over wine, those who go to search out mixed wine.

verses.rationale: Follow cup read form and sensual allure.
verses.before: Do not look at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly.
verses.after: Do not gaze at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not look at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly.

verses.before: In the end it bites like a serpent and stings like a viper.
verses.after: In the end it bites like a snake and strikes like a viper.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the end it bites like a serpent and stings like a viper.

verses.rationale: Choose strange things rather than women; note alternative.
verses.before: Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will speak perversities.
verses.after: Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will speak perversities.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will speak perversities.

verses.before: You will be like one lying down in the heart of the sea, like one lying at the top of a mast.
verses.after: You will be like someone lying in the heart of the sea, like someone lying at the top of a mast.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will be like one lying down in the heart of the sea, like one lying at the top of a mast.

verses.rationale: Preserve intoxicated speaker and returning appetite.
verses.before: “They struck me, but I was not hurt. They beat me, but I did not feel it. When will I wake up? I will seek another drink.”
verses.after: “They struck me, but I felt no pain; they beat me, but I did not know it. When will I wake up? I will seek another drink.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “They struck me, but I was not hurt. They beat me, but I did not feel it. When will I wake up? I will seek another drink.”

verses.before: Do not envy evil people, and do not desire to be with them,
verses.after: Do not envy evil men or desire their company,
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not envy evil people, and do not desire to be with them,

verses.rationale: Keep inner plotting and outward speech.
verses.before: for their hearts devise violence and their lips speak trouble.
verses.after: for their hearts devise violence and their lips speak trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: for their hearts devise violence and their lips speak trouble.

verses.before: By wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established.
verses.after: By wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
verses.tsw_comparator: By wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established.

verses.rationale: Keep furnished rooms rather than abstractions alone.
verses.before: Through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.
verses.after: by knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.

verses.before: A wise person is strong, and a person of knowledge increases strength.
verses.after: A wise man has strength; a knowledgeable man increases his power.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wise person is strong, and a person of knowledge increases strength.

verses.rationale: Keep military context and plural counsel.
verses.before: For by wise guidance you can wage war, and in an abundance of counselors there is deliverance.
verses.after: For with guidance you wage your war, and with many counselors comes deliverance.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by wise guidance you can wage war, and in an abundance of counselors there is deliverance.

verses.before: Wisdom is too high for a fool; at the gate they do not open their mouth.
verses.after: Wisdom is too high for a fool; at the gate he does not open his mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wisdom is too high for a fool; at the gate they do not open their mouth.

verses.before: Whoever plans to do evil will be called a schemer.
verses.after: One who plans to do evil will be called a master of schemes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever plans to do evil will be called a schemer.

verses.rationale: Retain human rather than divine audience.
verses.before: The scheme of folly is sin, and a scoffer is an abomination to humanity.
verses.after: Folly’s schemes are sin, and a scoffer is detestable to people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The scheme of folly is sin, and a scoffer is an abomination to humanity.

verses.before: If you become weak in the day of trouble, your strength is small.
verses.after: If you collapse on a day of trouble, your strength is small.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you become weak in the day of trouble, your strength is small.

verses.rationale: Keep active rescue of endangered people.
verses.before: Rescue those being taken away to death; hold back those staggering toward slaughter.
verses.after: Rescue those being taken away to death; hold back those staggering toward slaughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rescue those being taken away to death; hold back those staggering toward slaughter.

verses.rationale: Preserve plural excuse and accountability questions.
verses.before: If you say, “Look, we did not know this,” does not the one who weighs hearts understand? Does not the one who guards your life know? Will that one not repay each person according to their work?
verses.after: If you say, “Look, we did not know this,” does not the one who weighs hearts understand? Does not the guardian of your life know? Will he not repay each person according to his deeds?
verses.tsw_comparator: If you say, “Look, we did not know this,” does not the one who weighs hearts understand? Does not the one who guards your life know? Will that one not repay each person according to their work?

verses.before: My child, eat honey, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
verses.after: My son, eat honey, for it is good; honey from the comb is sweet to your taste.
verses.tsw_comparator: My child, eat honey, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.

verses.rationale: Retain analogy and repeated future promise.
verses.before: Know that wisdom is like this for your life; if you find it, there will be a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
verses.after: Know that wisdom is like this for your soul. If you find it, there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: Know that wisdom is like this for your life; if you find it, there will be a future, and your hope will not be cut off.

verses.before: Do not lie in wait like the wicked against the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy their resting place.
verses.after: Do not lie in wait, wicked one, against the home of the righteous; do not devastate his resting place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not lie in wait like the wicked against the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy their resting place.

verses.rationale: Keep seven and adversity rather than automatically sin.
verses.before: For though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again, but the wicked stumble in calamity.
verses.after: For the righteous fall seven times and rise again, but the wicked stumble in disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again, but the wicked stumble in calamity.

verses.before: Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when they stumble,
verses.after: Do not rejoice when your enemy falls; do not let your heart exult when he stumbles,
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when they stumble,

verses.rationale: Preserve counterintuitive withdrawal of wrath from enemy.
verses.before: lest the LORD see and it be evil in the LORD’s eyes, and the LORD turn anger away from them.
verses.after: or the LORD may see and be displeased and turn his anger away from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest the LORD see and it be evil in the LORD’s eyes, and the LORD turn anger away from them.

verses.before: Do not become agitated because of evildoers; do not envy the wicked.
verses.after: Do not burn with anger over evildoers; do not envy the wicked,
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not become agitated because of evildoers; do not envy the wicked.

verses.before: For there is no future for the evil person; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
verses.after: for the evil have no future; the lamp of the wicked will go out.
verses.tsw_comparator: For there is no future for the evil person; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

verses.rationale: Choose changers as rebels in royal context.
verses.before: My child, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with people who seek change through rebellion,
verses.after: My son, fear the LORD and the king; do not associate with those who rebel,
verses.tsw_comparator: My child, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with those who seek change through rebellion,

verses.rationale: Keep both referring to LORD and king with note.
verses.before: for their disaster will rise suddenly, and who knows the ruin that both may bring?
verses.after: for their disaster rises suddenly, and who knows the ruin that comes from them both?
verses.tsw_comparator: for their disaster will rise suddenly, and who knows the ruin that both may bring?

verses.rationale: Keep new collection label within verse.
verses.before: These also are sayings of the wise: Showing partiality in judgment is not good.
verses.after: These too are sayings of the wise. Showing partiality in judgment is not good.
verses.tsw_comparator: These also are sayings of the wise: Showing partiality in judgment is not good.

verses.rationale: Preserve judicial reversal and public reaction.
verses.before: Whoever says to the wicked, “You are righteous,” will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations.
verses.after: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent,” will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever says to the wicked, “You are righteous,” will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations.

verses.before: But it will go well with people who correct the wicked, and good blessing will come upon them.
verses.after: But it will go well with those who convict the guilty; a good blessing will come upon them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But it will go well with those who correct the wicked, and good blessing will come upon them.

verses.before: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
verses.after: An honest answer is a kiss on the lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.

verses.rationale: Keep agricultural order and house ambiguity.
verses.before: Prepare your work outside and make it ready for yourself in the field; afterward build your house.
verses.after: Prepare your work outside; get your fields ready. After that, build your house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Prepare your work outside and make it ready for yourself in the field; afterward build your house.

verses.rationale: Preserve rhetorical question in second line.

verses.after: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause; would you deceive with your lips?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.

verses.before: Do not say, “As they did to me, so I will do to them; I will repay the person according to their work.”
verses.after: Do not say, “I will do to him what he did to me; I will repay the man according to his deeds.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not say, “As they did to me, so I will do to them; I will repay the person according to their work.”

verses.before: I passed by the field of a lazy person, by the vineyard of one lacking sense.
verses.after: I passed by a sluggard’s field, by the vineyard of a person without sense.
verses.tsw_comparator: I passed by the field of a lazy person, by the vineyard of one lacking sense.

verses.after: Thorns had grown over it all; nettles covered its surface, and its stone wall was broken down.
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, it was all overgrown with thorns; nettles covered its surface, and its stone wall was broken down.

verses.before: Then I looked and took it to heart; I saw and received discipline:
verses.after: I looked and took it to heart; I saw and received discipline:

verses.before: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,

verses.before: and your poverty will come like a robber and your need like an armed warrior.
verses.after: and poverty will come upon you like a prowler, need like a man with a shield.
verses.tsw_comparator: and your poverty will come like a robber and your need like an armed warrior.

verses.after: These too are proverbs of Solomon, copied by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied.

verses.after: It is God’s glory to conceal a matter; it is kings’ glory to search a matter out.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, and the glory of kings to search a matter out.

verses.after: The heavens in height, the earth in depth, and the heart of kings cannot be searched out.

verses.before: Remove the dross from silver, and material comes forth for the silversmith.
verses.after: Remove the dross from silver, and a vessel comes forth for the smith.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remove the dross from silver, and material comes forth for the silversmith.

verses.after: Remove the wicked from a king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and the throne will be established in righteousness.

verses.after: Better to be told, “Come up here,” than to be brought low before a noble. What your eyes have seen,

verses.after: Argue your case with your neighbor, but do not reveal another person’s confidence,
verses.tsw_comparator: Argue your case with your neighbor, but do not reveal another person’s secret,

verses.after: or the hearer may disgrace you, and your bad reputation will not go away.

verses.after: Golden apples in silver settings— such is a word spoken at the right moment.

verses.after: A gold ring, an ornament of fine gold— such is a wise correction to a listening ear.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a gold ring or an ornament of fine gold is a wise correction to a listening ear.

verses.before: Like clouds and wind without rain is one who boasts of a gift never given.

verses.after: Through patience a ruler is persuaded; a gentle tongue breaks a bone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through patience a ruler may be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
