verses.before: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest they become weary of you and hate you.
verses.after: Let your visits to your neighbor’s house be rare, or he will grow tired of you and hate you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest they become weary of you and hate you.

verses.rationale: Keep three weapons and judicial harm.
verses.before: Like a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow is one who gives false testimony against a neighbor.
verses.after: A club, a sword, a sharpened arrow— such is one who gives false testimony against his neighbor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow is one who gives false testimony against a neighbor.

verses.before: Like a broken tooth or an unsteady foot is trust in an unfaithful person in a day of trouble.
verses.after: A broken tooth and an unsteady foot— such is trust in a faithless person on a day of trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a broken tooth or an unsteady foot is trust in an unfaithful person in a day of trouble.

verses.rationale: Keep unsettling comparisons without replacing chemical substance.
verses.before: Like taking off a garment on a cold day, or vinegar poured on soda, is one who sings songs to a troubled heart.
verses.after: Taking off a garment on a cold day, pouring vinegar on soda— such is singing songs to a troubled heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like taking off a garment on a cold day, or vinegar poured on soda, is one who sings songs to a troubled heart.

verses.before: If your enemy is hungry, give them bread to eat; if they are thirsty, give them water to drink,
verses.after: If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: If your enemy is hungry, give them bread to eat; if they are thirsty, give them water to drink,

verses.before: for you will heap burning coals upon their head, and the LORD will reward you.
verses.after: For you will heap coals on his head, and the LORD will repay you.
verses.tsw_comparator: for you will heap burning coals upon their head, and the LORD will reward you.

verses.before: A north wind brings rain, and a secretive tongue brings angry faces.
verses.after: The north wind brings rain, and a secretive tongue brings angry faces.
verses.tsw_comparator: A north wind brings rain, and a secretive tongue brings angry faces.

verses.before: Better to live on a corner of a roof than share a house with a quarrelsome spouse.
verses.after: Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better to live on a corner of a roof than share a house with a quarrelsome spouse.

verses.before: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
verses.after: Cold water to a weary soul— such is good news from a distant land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.

verses.before: Like a muddied spring or a polluted fountain is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.
verses.after: A muddied spring, a ruined fountain— such is a righteous person giving way before the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a muddied spring or a polluted fountain is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.

verses.rationale: Carry first-line negation into compressed glory clause; document unexpressed negative and positive alternative.
verses.before: It is not good to eat too much honey, nor is seeking one’s own glory glorious.
verses.after: Eating much honey is not good; pursuing your own honor brings no honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is not good to eat too much honey, nor is seeking one’s own glory glorious.

verses.before: Like a city broken into and without walls is a person without self-control.
verses.after: A breached city without a wall— such is a person who cannot restrain his spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a city broken into and without walls is a person without self-control.

verses.before: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
verses.after: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor does not suit a fool.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.

verses.rationale: Choose written negative; note read form to him.
verses.before: Like a sparrow flitting and a swallow flying, so a curse without cause does not come to rest.
verses.after: Like a fluttering bird, like a flying swallow, a groundless curse does not come to rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a sparrow flitting and a swallow flying, so a curse without cause does not come to rest.

verses.rationale: Keep animal and human restraint comparison.
verses.before: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools.
verses.after: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools.
verses.tsw_comparator: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools.

verses.rationale: Retain first half of deliberate paired tension.
verses.before: Do not answer a fool according to their folly, lest you also become like them.
verses.after: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you too will become like him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not answer a fool according to their folly, lest you also become like them.

verses.before: Answer a fool according to their folly, lest they become wise in their own eyes.
verses.after: Answer a fool according to his folly, or he will become wise in his own eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Answer a fool according to their folly, lest they become wise in their own eyes.

verses.before: Whoever sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off their own feet and drinks violence.
verses.after: Sending a message by a fool is cutting off your feet and drinking violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off their own feet and drinks violence.

verses.rationale: Preserve disability comparison without substituting another image.
verses.before: Like the legs of the lame hanging loose is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.after: Like the dangling legs of someone unable to walk is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like the legs of the lame hanging loose is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

verses.before: Like tying a stone into a sling is giving honor to a fool.
verses.after: Like binding a stone in a sling is giving honor to a fool.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like tying a stone into a sling is giving honor to a fool.

verses.before: Like a thorn that enters the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.after: Like a thorn in a drunkard’s hand is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a thorn that enters the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

verses.rationale: Choose archer reading of highly difficult verse; flag alternatives.
verses.before: Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a fool or whoever happens to pass by.
verses.after: Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a fool or hires passersby.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a fool or whoever happens to pass by.

verses.before: Like a dog that returns to its vomit is a fool who repeats folly.
verses.after: Like a dog returning to its vomit, a fool repeats his folly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a dog that returns to its vomit is a fool who repeats folly.

verses.before: Do you see someone wise in their own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for them.
verses.after: Have you seen someone wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you see someone wise in their own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for them.

verses.before: The lazy person says, “There is a lion in the road! A lion in the public square!”
verses.after: A sluggard says, “A lion is on the road! A lion is in the streets!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The lazy person says, “There is a lion in the road! A lion in the public square!”

verses.before: As a door turns on its hinges, so the lazy person turns on the bed.
verses.after: A door turns on its hinge, and a sluggard on his bed.
verses.tsw_comparator: As a door turns on its hinges, so the lazy person turns on the bed.

verses.rationale: Retain hyperbole and weariness distinct from 19:24.
verses.before: The lazy person buries a hand in the dish and is too weary to bring it back to the mouth.
verses.after: A sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he is too weary to bring it back to his mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lazy person buries a hand in the dish and is too weary to bring it back to the mouth.

verses.before: The lazy person is wiser in their own eyes than seven people who can answer sensibly.
verses.after: A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven people who answer sensibly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lazy person is wiser in their own eyes than seven people who can answer sensibly.

verses.before: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in someone else’s quarrel.
verses.after: Like grabbing a dog by the ears is a passerby who gets angry over someone else’s quarrel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in someone else’s quarrel.

verses.before: Like a madman who shoots firebrands, arrows, and death,
verses.after: Like a madman shooting firebrands, arrows, and death,
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a madman who shoots firebrands, arrows, and death,

verses.before: so is one who deceives a neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
verses.after: so is someone who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only playing!”
verses.tsw_comparator: so is one who deceives a neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”

verses.before: Without wood the fire goes out; without a gossip conflict quiets down.
verses.after: Without wood a fire goes out; without a whisperer a quarrel grows quiet.
verses.tsw_comparator: Without wood the fire goes out; without a gossip conflict quiets down.

verses.rationale: Follow quarrels read form and fuel list.
verses.before: As charcoal is for hot embers and wood for fire, so a contentious person is for kindling conflict.
verses.after: Charcoal for embers, wood for fire, and a quarrelsome person for kindling conflict.
verses.tsw_comparator: As charcoal is for hot embers and wood for fire, so a contentious person is for kindling conflict.

verses.before: The words of a gossip are like delicious morsels; they go down to the innermost parts.
verses.after: A whisperer’s words are like tasty morsels; they go down into the innermost belly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of a gossip are like delicious morsels; they go down to the innermost parts.

verses.rationale: Keep pinned silver dross and burning lips, not emend smooth.
verses.before: Like silver glaze covering an earthen vessel are smooth lips with an evil heart.
verses.after: Silver dross coating earthenware— such are burning lips with an evil heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like silver glaze covering an earthen vessel are smooth lips with an evil heart.

verses.before: One who hates disguises it with their lips, but within themselves they store deception.
verses.after: A hater disguises himself with his lips while storing up deceit within.
verses.tsw_comparator: One who hates disguises it with their lips, but within themselves they store deception.

verses.before: When they make their voice gracious, do not trust them, for seven abominations are in their heart.
verses.after: When his voice grows gracious, do not trust him, for seven detestable things are in his heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they make their voice gracious, do not trust them, for seven abominations are in their heart.

verses.before: Though hatred is covered with deception, its wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
verses.after: Though hatred is covered by deception, his evil will be exposed in the assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though hatred is covered with deception, its wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

verses.before: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone will have it roll back upon them.
verses.after: Whoever digs a pit falls into it; a stone rolls back on the one who rolls it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone will have it roll back upon them.

verses.before: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth brings ruin.
verses.after: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a smooth mouth brings ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth brings ruin.

verses.before: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
verses.after: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day will bring to birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.

verses.before: Let another praise you and not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.
verses.after: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth; a stranger, not your own lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let another praise you and not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.

verses.before: A stone is heavy and sand is weighty, but the provocation of a fool is heavier than both.
verses.after: Stone is heavy and sand a burden, but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
verses.tsw_comparator: A stone is heavy and sand is weighty, but the provocation of a fool is heavier than both.

verses.before: Wrath is cruel and anger is a flood, but who can stand before jealousy?
verses.after: Fury is cruel and anger a flood, but who can stand before jealousy?
verses.tsw_comparator: Wrath is cruel and anger is a flood, but who can stand before jealousy?

verses.before: Better is open correction than love kept hidden.
verses.after: Better an open correction than a hidden love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is open correction than love kept hidden.

verses.rationale: Retain harmful-looking loyalty and excessive affection.
verses.before: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are excessive.
verses.after: A friend’s wounds are trustworthy; an enemy’s kisses are plentiful.
verses.tsw_comparator: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are excessive.

verses.before: A satisfied person tramples honey, but to a hungry person even bitterness is sweet.
verses.after: One who is full tramples honeycomb underfoot; to the hungry even bitter things are sweet.
verses.tsw_comparator: A satisfied person tramples honey, but to a hungry person even bitterness is sweet.

verses.before: Like a bird wandering from its nest is a person wandering from home.
verses.after: Like a bird wandering from its nest is a person wandering from home.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a bird wandering from its nest is a person wandering from home.

verses.rationale: Choose source-of-sweetness reading; note compressed syntax.
verses.before: Oil and incense make the heart glad, and the sweetness of a friend comes from heartfelt counsel.
verses.after: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart; a friend’s sweetness comes from heartfelt counsel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Oil and incense make the heart glad, and the sweetness of a friend comes from heartfelt counsel.

verses.rationale: Follow friend read form and preserve comparative accessibility.
verses.before: Do not abandon your friend or your parent’s friend; do not enter your sibling’s house in the day of your disaster. Better a nearby neighbor than a distant sibling.
verses.after: Do not abandon your friend or your father’s friend. Do not go to your brother’s house on your day of disaster; better a nearby neighbor than a distant brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not abandon your friend or your parent’s friend; do not enter your sibling’s house in the day of your disaster. Better a nearby neighbor than a distant sibling.

verses.before: Be wise, my child, and make my heart glad, so that I may answer the one who reproaches me.
verses.after: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so I can answer the one who reproaches me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be wise, my child, and make my heart glad, so that I may answer the one who reproaches me.

verses.before: The prudent see danger and hide themselves; the simple pass on and suffer for it.
verses.after: The prudent see danger and hide, but the inexperienced go on and suffer for it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prudent see danger and hide themselves; the simple pass on and suffer for it.

verses.rationale: Match 20:16’s read form now written in source.
verses.before: Take the garment of one who becomes surety for a stranger; hold it as security for an outsider.
verses.after: Take the garment of one who guarantees a stranger’s debt; hold it as a pledge when he guarantees an outsider woman’s debt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take the garment of one who becomes surety for a stranger; hold it as security for an outsider.

verses.before: Whoever blesses a neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning may have it counted as a curse.
verses.after: Whoever blesses his neighbor loudly at dawn will have it counted as a curse.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever blesses a neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning may have it counted as a curse.

verses.before: A continual dripping on a rainy day and a quarrelsome spouse are alike.
verses.after: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a quarrelsome wife are alike.
verses.tsw_comparator: A continual dripping on a rainy day and a quarrelsome spouse are alike.

verses.rationale: Choose grasp sense of difficult final verb; note uncertainty.
verses.before: Whoever would restrain such a person restrains the wind and grasps oil with the hand.
verses.after: Restraining her is restraining the wind, trying to grasp oil in one’s right hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever would restrain such a person restrains the wind and grasps oil with the hand.

verses.rationale: Retain face image rather than generic improvement alone.
verses.before: Iron sharpens iron, and one person sharpens the face of another.
verses.after: Iron sharpens iron, and a person sharpens his neighbor’s face.
verses.tsw_comparator: Iron sharpens iron, and one person sharpens the face of another.

verses.before: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever guards a master will be honored.
verses.after: Whoever tends a fig tree eats its fruit; whoever guards his master will be honored.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever guards a master will be honored.

verses.rationale: Preserve compressed reflection comparison and open referent.
verses.before: As water reflects a face to a face, so a human heart reflects the person.
verses.after: As water reflects face to face, so a human heart reflects a person.
verses.tsw_comparator: As water reflects a face to a face, so a human heart reflects the person.

verses.rationale: Follow Abaddon read form; keep repeated appetite.
verses.before: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and the eyes of humanity are never satisfied.
verses.after: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and human eyes are never satisfied.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and the eyes of humanity are never satisfied.

verses.rationale: Keep praise’s ambiguous relation to person.
verses.before: The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, and a person is tested by the praise they receive.
verses.after: A crucible is for silver and a furnace for gold, and a person is tested by his praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, and a person is tested by the praise they receive.

verses.rationale: Preserve violent absurdity rather than sanitize.
verses.before: Even if you crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with crushed grain, their folly will not depart.
verses.after: Even if you pound a fool in a mortar among crushed grain with a pestle, his folly will not leave him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even if you crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with crushed grain, their folly will not depart.

verses.before: Know well the condition of your flocks; give careful attention to your herds,
verses.after: Know well the condition of your flock; pay close attention to your herds,
verses.tsw_comparator: Know well the condition of your flocks; give careful attention to your herds,

verses.rationale: Follow generation conjunction read form and retain question.
verses.before: for riches do not last forever, nor does a crown endure from generation to generation.
verses.after: for wealth does not last forever. Does a crown endure from generation to generation?
verses.tsw_comparator: for riches do not last forever, nor does a crown endure from generation to generation.

verses.rationale: Keep agricultural sequence without inventing season dates.
verses.before: When the hay is removed and new grass appears and the vegetation of the hills is gathered,
verses.after: The grass is taken away, fresh growth appears, and the mountain plants are gathered.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the hay is removed and new grass appears and the vegetation of the hills is gathered,

verses.before: lambs will provide your clothing, and goats the price of a field,
verses.after: Lambs will provide your clothing, and goats the price of a field.
verses.tsw_comparator: lambs will provide your clothing, and goats the price of a field,

verses.rationale: Retain female household workers and sufficiency.
verses.before: and there will be enough goat’s milk for your food, for the food of your household, and provision for your servants.
verses.after: There will be enough goats’ milk for your food, for your household’s food, and for the livelihood of your young women.
verses.tsw_comparator: and there will be enough goat’s milk for your food, for the food of your household, and provision for your servants.

verses.before: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are confident like a lion.
verses.after: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are confident as a young lion.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are confident like a lion.

verses.rationale: Preserve political instability and difficult order term.
verses.before: Because of a land’s transgression its rulers become many, but through a person of understanding and knowledge stability continues.
verses.after: When a land rebels, its rulers multiply; with an understanding, knowledgeable person, order endures.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of a land’s transgression its rulers become many, but through a person of understanding and knowledge stability continues.

verses.rationale: Keep pinned poor rather than conjectured ruler.
verses.before: A poor person who oppresses the poor is like sweeping rain that leaves no food.
verses.after: A poor man who oppresses the needy is like a sweeping rain that leaves no bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: A poor person who oppresses the poor is like sweeping rain that leaves no food.

verses.rationale: Retain Torah as instruction and active opposition.
verses.before: People who abandon instruction praise the wicked, but people who keep instruction struggle against them.
verses.after: Those who abandon instruction praise the wicked; those who keep instruction contend with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who abandon instruction praise the wicked, but those who keep instruction struggle against them.

verses.rationale: Keep justice as scope of all.
verses.before: Evil people do not understand justice, but people who seek the LORD understand it fully.
verses.after: Evil men do not understand justice; those who seek the LORD understand it fully.
verses.tsw_comparator: Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD understand it fully.

verses.before: Better is a poor person who walks in integrity than a rich person whose ways are crooked.
verses.after: Better a poor person who walks with integrity than a rich person whose ways are crooked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is a poor person who walks in integrity than a rich person whose ways are crooked.

verses.before: Whoever keeps instruction is a discerning child, but a companion of gluttons brings shame to a parent.
verses.after: A son who keeps instruction has understanding; a companion of gluttons brings his father shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever keeps instruction is a discerning child, but a companion of gluttons brings shame to a parent.

verses.rationale: Follow read form and preserve transfer to benefactor.
verses.before: Whoever increases wealth through interest and excessive profit gathers it for one who shows favor to the poor.
verses.after: Whoever increases wealth through interest and extra charges gathers it for someone who shows mercy to the poor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever increases wealth through interest and excessive profit gathers it for one who shows favor to the poor.

verses.before: Whoever turns away an ear from hearing instruction, even their prayer is an abomination.
verses.after: Whoever turns his ear away from hearing instruction— even his prayer is detestable.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever turns away an ear from hearing instruction, even their prayer is an abomination.

verses.rationale: Keep perpetrator’s own trap and positive contrast.
verses.before: Whoever leads the upright into an evil way will fall into their own pit, but the blameless will inherit good.
verses.after: Whoever leads the upright astray onto an evil road will fall into his own pit, but those of integrity will inherit good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever leads the upright into an evil way will fall into their own pit, but the blameless will inherit good.

verses.before: A rich person is wise in their own eyes, but a discerning poor person sees through them.
verses.after: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor person with understanding sees through him.
verses.tsw_comparator: A rich person is wise in their own eyes, but a discerning poor person sees through them.

verses.before: When the righteous rejoice, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, people hide themselves.
verses.after: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; when the wicked rise, people hide.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the righteous rejoice, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, people hide themselves.

verses.rationale: Distinguish own-offense concealment from forgiving another’s.
verses.before: Whoever conceals transgressions will not prosper, but whoever confesses and abandons them will receive mercy.
verses.after: Whoever covers his offenses will not prosper; whoever confesses and abandons them will receive mercy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever conceals transgressions will not prosper, but whoever confesses and abandons them will receive mercy.

verses.rationale: Render continual fear as reverence; note unspecified object.
verses.before: Blessed is the one who is always reverent, but whoever hardens their heart falls into disaster.
verses.after: Happy is the person who remains reverent, but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed is the one who is always reverent, but whoever hardens their heart falls into disaster.

verses.before: Like a roaring lion and a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
verses.after: A roaring lion, a charging bear— such is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a roaring lion and a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people.

verses.before: A ruler who lacks understanding is a great oppressor, but one who hates unjust gain will prolong days.
verses.after: A ruler without understanding is a great oppressor; one who hates unjust gain will prolong his days.
verses.tsw_comparator: A ruler who lacks understanding is a great oppressor, but one who hates unjust gain will prolong days.

verses.rationale: Keep bloodguilt, death, and hard prohibition.
verses.before: A person burdened with the blood of another will be a fugitive until death; let no one support them.
verses.after: A person burdened with another’s lifeblood will flee to the Pit; let no one support him.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person burdened with the blood of another will be a fugitive until death; let no one support them.

verses.rationale: Choose at once sense; note in one of them alternative.
verses.before: Whoever walks in integrity will be saved, but one crooked in two ways will fall suddenly.
verses.after: Whoever walks with integrity will be delivered; one whose ways are crooked will fall suddenly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever walks in integrity will be saved, but one crooked in two ways will fall suddenly.

verses.before: Whoever works the land will have plenty of bread, but whoever pursues empty things will have plenty of poverty.
verses.after: Whoever works his land has enough bread; whoever chases empty pursuits has enough poverty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever works the land will have plenty of bread, but whoever pursues empty things will have plenty of poverty.

verses.before: A faithful person will abound with blessings, but whoever hurries to become rich will not go unpunished.
verses.after: A trustworthy person has abundant blessings; one who hurries to grow rich will not go unpunished.
verses.tsw_comparator: A faithful person will abound with blessings, but whoever hurries to become rich will not go unpunished.

verses.rationale: Retain small inducement without condoning it.
verses.before: Showing partiality is not good, yet for a piece of bread a person may transgress.
verses.after: Showing partiality is not good, yet a man may do wrong for a piece of bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: Showing partiality is not good, yet for a piece of bread a person may transgress.

verses.rationale: Keep evil-eye idiom and approaching reversal.
verses.before: One with a stingy eye hurries after wealth and does not know that poverty will come upon them.
verses.after: A stingy man hurries after wealth, unaware that need is coming upon him.
verses.tsw_comparator: One with a stingy eye hurries after wealth and does not know that poverty will come upon them.

verses.before: Whoever corrects a person will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.
verses.after: Whoever corrects a person will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever corrects a person will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.

verses.before: Whoever robs father or mother and says, “It is no transgression,” is companion to a destroyer.
verses.after: Whoever robs his father or mother and says, “It is no offense,” is companion to a destroyer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever robs father or mother and says, “It is no transgression,” is companion to a destroyer.

verses.before: A greedy person stirs up conflict, but whoever trusts in the LORD will flourish.
verses.after: A greedy person stirs up conflict, but one who trusts in the LORD will flourish.
verses.tsw_comparator: A greedy person stirs up conflict, but whoever trusts in the LORD will flourish.

verses.before: Whoever trusts in their own heart is a fool, but whoever walks in wisdom will be delivered.
verses.after: Whoever trusts his own heart is a fool; whoever walks in wisdom will escape.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever trusts in their own heart is a fool, but whoever walks in wisdom will be delivered.

verses.before: Whoever gives to the poor will have no lack, but whoever hides their eyes will receive many curses.
verses.after: Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing; whoever closes his eyes will have many curses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever gives to the poor will have no lack, but whoever hides their eyes will receive many curses.

verses.before: When the wicked rise, people hide themselves, but when they perish, the righteous increase.
verses.after: When the wicked rise, people hide; when they perish, the righteous increase.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the wicked rise, people hide themselves, but when they perish, the righteous increase.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily stubbornness and irreversible consequence.
verses.before: One who is often corrected yet stiffens the neck will suddenly be broken beyond healing.
verses.after: One often corrected who stiffens his neck will suddenly be broken beyond healing.
verses.tsw_comparator: One who is often corrected yet stiffens the neck will suddenly be broken beyond healing.

verses.before: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verses.after: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; when a wicked person rules, the people groan.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.

verses.rationale: Keep masculine relationship and economic loss.
verses.before: Whoever loves wisdom makes a parent glad, but one who keeps company with prostitutes squanders wealth.
verses.after: A man who loves wisdom brings his father joy; a companion of prostitutes wastes wealth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever loves wisdom makes a parent glad, but one who keeps company with prostitutes squanders wealth.

verses.rationale: Retain levies/contributions ambiguity rather than bribes only.
verses.before: By justice a king establishes the land, but one who demands gifts tears it down.
verses.after: Through justice a king makes a land stand firm; a man who exacts contributions tears it down.
verses.tsw_comparator: By justice a king establishes the land, but one who demands gifts tears it down.

verses.before: A person who flatters a neighbor spreads a net for their feet.
verses.after: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person who flatters a neighbor spreads a net for their feet.

verses.before: An evil person is caught by their transgression, but the righteous sing and rejoice.
verses.after: An evil man’s offense is a snare, but the righteous sing and rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: An evil person is caught by their transgression, but the righteous sing and rejoice.

verses.rationale: Keep judicial concern, not information alone.
verses.before: The righteous know the rights of the poor; the wicked do not understand such knowledge.
verses.after: The righteous know the cause of the poor; the wicked have no understanding of such knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous know the rights of the poor; the wicked do not understand such knowledge.

verses.before: Scoffers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
verses.after: Scoffers set a city ablaze; the wise turn anger away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Scoffers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.

verses.rationale: Leave ambiguous actor of rage/laughter unassigned.
verses.before: If a wise person enters a dispute with a fool, the fool rages and laughs, and there is no rest.
verses.after: When a wise man goes to court with a fool, there is raging and laughing, but no quiet.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a wise person enters a dispute with a fool, the fool rages and laughs, and there is no rest.

verses.rationale: Choose protective seeking; note difficult syntax.
verses.before: Bloodthirsty people hate the blameless, but the upright seek to preserve their life.
verses.after: Bloodthirsty men hate one of integrity, but the upright seek to preserve his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bloodthirsty people hate the blameless, but the upright seek to preserve their life.

verses.before: A fool gives full vent to the spirit, but the wise calmly hold it back.
verses.after: A fool lets out all his anger; a wise person holds it back and quiets it.
verses.tsw_comparator: A fool gives full vent to the spirit, but the wise calmly hold it back.

verses.before: If a ruler listens to falsehood, all the ruler’s servants become wicked.
verses.after: When a ruler listens to falsehood, all his attendants become wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a ruler listens to falsehood, all the ruler’s servants become wicked.

verses.before: The poor person and the oppressor meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
verses.after: The poor and the oppressor meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
verses.tsw_comparator: The poor person and the oppressor meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of both.

verses.rationale: Keep justice for poor as foundation.
verses.before: If a king judges the poor with faithfulness, the throne will be established forever.
verses.after: A king who judges the poor faithfully will have his throne established forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a king judges the poor with faithfulness, the throne will be established forever.

verses.rationale: Retain physical rod and mother specifically.
verses.before: The rod and correction give wisdom, but a child left without guidance brings shame to a mother.
verses.after: The rod and correction give wisdom; a youth left to himself brings his mother shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rod and correction give wisdom, but a child left without guidance brings shame to a mother.

verses.before: When the wicked increase, transgression increases, but the righteous will see their downfall.
verses.after: When the wicked increase, offenses increase, but the righteous will see their downfall.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the wicked increase, transgression increases, but the righteous will see their downfall.

verses.before: Discipline your child, and they will give you rest and bring delight to your life.
verses.after: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
verses.tsw_comparator: Discipline your child, and they will give you rest and bring delight to your life.

verses.rationale: Keep revelation rather than managerial vision.
verses.before: Where there is no vision, a people cast off restraint, but blessed is the one who keeps instruction.
verses.after: Without prophetic vision, a people casts off restraint; happy is the one who keeps instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Where there is no vision, a people cast off restraint, but blessed is the one who keeps instruction.

verses.rationale: Retain coercive ancient relationship without approving it in notes.
verses.before: A servant will not be corrected by words alone; though understanding, there may be no response.
verses.after: A servant is not disciplined by words alone; though he understands, there is no response.
verses.tsw_comparator: A servant will not be corrected by words alone; though understanding, there may be no response.

verses.before: Do you see someone hasty in speech? There is more hope for a fool than for them.
verses.after: Have you seen someone hasty in speech? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you see someone hasty in speech? There is more hope for a fool than for them.

verses.rationale: Choose son sense of rare manon; flag uncertainty.
verses.before: Whoever pampers a servant from youth may find in the end that the servant claims the household.
verses.after: One who pampers his servant from youth will find him acting as a son in the end.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever pampers a servant from youth may find in the end that the servant claims the household.

verses.before: An angry person stirs up conflict, and one given to rage commits many transgressions.
verses.after: An angry man stirs up conflict; a furious man commits many offenses.
verses.tsw_comparator: An angry person stirs up conflict, and one given to rage commits many transgressions.

verses.before: A person’s pride will bring them low, but one humble in spirit will obtain honor.
verses.after: A person’s pride brings him low, but a lowly spirit holds on to honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: A person’s pride will bring them low, but one humble in spirit will obtain honor.

verses.rationale: Explain legal oath without losing complicit silence.
verses.before: Whoever shares with a thief hates their own life; they hear the oath but disclose nothing.
verses.after: A thief’s partner hates his own life; he hears the oath of testimony but says nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever shares with a thief hates their own life; they hear the oath but disclose nothing.

verses.before: Fear of another person sets a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely.
verses.after: Fear of people lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is safe on high.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fear of another person sets a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely.

verses.rationale: Keep distinction of access and justice.
verses.before: Many seek the face of a ruler, but a person’s justice comes from the LORD.
verses.after: Many seek a ruler’s favor, but a person’s justice comes from the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many seek the face of a ruler, but a person’s justice comes from the LORD.

verses.before: An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is an abomination to the wicked.
verses.after: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is an abomination to the wicked.

verses.rationale: Preserve pinned names; note alternate parsing and Massa possibility.
verses.before: The words of Agur son of Jakeh, the oracle. The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
verses.after: The words of Agur son of Jakeh. The oracle. The man’s declaration to Ithiel— to Ithiel and Ucal:
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of Agur son of Jakeh, the oracle. The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:

verses.before: Surely I am more ignorant than any person, and I do not have human understanding.
verses.after: Surely I am more brutish than anyone; I do not have human understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely I am more ignorant than any person, and I do not have human understanding.

verses.rationale: Carry negation across parallel; note plural holy ones.
verses.before: I have not learned wisdom, nor do I possess knowledge of the Holy One.
verses.after: I have not learned wisdom, nor do I have knowledge of the Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have not learned wisdom, nor do I possess knowledge of the Holy One.

verses.rationale: Preserve all questions and ironic challenge without later identification.
verses.before: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of the hands? Who has wrapped the waters in a garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is this one’s name, and what is the name of the son? Surely you know.
verses.after: Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in his hands? Who has wrapped the waters in a garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name? Surely you know!
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of the hands? Who has wrapped the waters in a garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is this one’s name, and what is the name of the son? Surely you know.

verses.before: Every word of God is refined; God is a shield to people who take refuge.
verses.after: Every word of God is refined; he is a shield to those who seek refuge in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every word of God is refined; God is a shield to those who take refuge.

verses.before: Do not add to God’s words, lest God correct you and you be found a liar.
verses.after: Do not add to his words, or he will correct you and you will be exposed as a liar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not add to God’s words, lest God correct you and you be found a liar.

verses.before: Two things I ask of you; do not withhold them from me before I die:
verses.after: Two things I ask of you; do not withhold them from me before I die:
verses.tsw_comparator: Two things I ask of you; do not withhold them from me before I die:

verses.rationale: Retain both economic limits and allotted food.
verses.before: Keep falsehood and lying speech far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread appointed for me,
verses.after: Keep falsehood and lying words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor wealth; feed me with the bread allotted to me,
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep falsehood and lying speech far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread appointed for me,

verses.before: lest I become full and deny you and say, “Who is the LORD?” or lest I become poor and steal and profane the name of my God.
verses.after: or I may be full and deny you, saying, “Who is the LORD?” Or I may become poor and steal, and misuse the name of my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest I become full and deny you and say, “Who is the LORD?” or lest I become poor and steal and profane the name of my God.

verses.rationale: Follow master read form; retain servant’s agency.
verses.before: Do not slander a servant to a master, lest the servant curse you and you be found guilty.
verses.after: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he may curse you and you will bear guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not slander a servant to a master, lest the servant curse you and you be found guilty.

verses.before: There is a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother.
verses.after: There is a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother;
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother.

verses.before: There is a generation pure in its own eyes yet not washed from its filth.
verses.after: a generation pure in its own eyes, yet not washed of its filth;
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a generation pure in its own eyes yet not washed from its filth.

verses.before: There is a generation— how high are its eyes, how lifted its eyelids!
verses.after: a generation—how haughty its eyes, how high its eyelids rise!
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a generation— how high are its eyes, how lifted its eyelids!

verses.before: There is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, to devour the poor from the earth and the needy from humanity.
verses.after: a generation with swords for teeth and knives for jaws, devouring the afflicted from the land and the needy from humankind.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, to devour the poor from the earth and the needy from humanity.

verses.rationale: Keep numbers, personification, and ascending formula.
verses.before: The leech has two daughters: “Give!” “Give!” Three things are never satisfied; four never say, “Enough”:
verses.after: The leech has two daughters: “Give! Give!” Three things are never satisfied; four never say, “Enough”:
verses.tsw_comparator: The leech has two daughters: “Give!” “Give!” Three things are never satisfied; four never say, “Enough”:

verses.before: Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, “Enough.”
verses.after: Sheol, the barren womb, the land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, “Enough.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, “Enough.”

verses.before: The eye that mocks a father and despises obedience to a mother— the ravens of the valley will peck it out, and the young eagles will eat it.
verses.after: The eye that mocks a father and despises obedience to a mother— ravens of the valley will peck it out, and young eagles will eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The eye that mocks a father and despises obedience to a mother— the ravens of the valley will peck it out, and the young eagles will eat it.

verses.rationale: Follow four read form and wonder.
verses.before: Three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand:
verses.after: Three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand:
verses.tsw_comparator: Three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand:

verses.rationale: Keep four repeated ways without reducing final sexual ambiguity.
verses.before: the way of an eagle in the heavens, the way of a serpent upon a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.
verses.after: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: the way of an eagle in the heavens, the way of a serpent upon a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.

verses.before: Such is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, “I have done nothing wrong.”
verses.after: This is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, “I have done nothing wrong.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Such is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, “I have done nothing wrong.”

verses.before: Under three things the earth trembles, and under four it cannot bear up:
verses.after: Under three things the earth trembles; under four it cannot bear up:
verses.tsw_comparator: Under three things the earth trembles, and under four it cannot bear up:

verses.rationale: Retain social reversals, not modern endorsement.
verses.before: a servant when he becomes king, a fool when filled with food,
verses.after: a servant who becomes king, a fool who has his fill of bread,
verses.tsw_comparator: a servant when he becomes king, a fool when filled with food,

verses.rationale: Preserve hated, not inherently hateful, and slavery.
verses.before: an unloved woman when she is married, and a servant woman when she inherits her mistress.
verses.after: a hated woman who marries, and a slave woman who succeeds her mistress.
verses.tsw_comparator: an unloved woman when she is married, and a servant woman when she inherits her mistress.

verses.before: Four things are small on the earth, yet they are exceedingly wise:
verses.after: Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise:
verses.tsw_comparator: Four things are small on the earth, yet they are exceedingly wise:

verses.before: ants are not a strong people, yet they prepare their food in summer;
verses.after: ants are a people without strength, yet they prepare their food in summer;
verses.tsw_comparator: ants are not a strong people, yet they prepare their food in summer;

verses.rationale: Keep rock-dwelling animal and people image.
verses.before: rock badgers are not a mighty people, yet they make their homes among the rocks;
verses.after: rock badgers are a people without power, yet they make their homes in the cliff;
verses.tsw_comparator: rock badgers are not a mighty people, yet they make their homes among the rocks;

verses.before: locusts have no king, yet all of them go out in ranks;
verses.after: locusts have no king, yet they all advance in ranks;
verses.tsw_comparator: locusts have no king, yet all of them go out in ranks;

verses.rationale: Choose catchable lizard reading; note gripping alternative.
verses.before: a lizard can be caught in the hands, yet it is found in royal palaces.
verses.after: a lizard can be caught in the hands, yet it is found in kings’ palaces.
verses.tsw_comparator: a lizard can be caught in the hands, yet it is found in royal palaces.

verses.rationale: Keep second animal list’s numerical structure.
verses.before: Three things are stately in their stride, and four are stately in their movement:
verses.after: Three things have a stately stride; four move with dignity:
verses.tsw_comparator: Three things are stately in their stride, and four are stately in their movement:

verses.before: the lion, mighty among animals, which does not turn back before anything;
verses.after: the lion, mighty among beasts, which retreats before nothing;
verses.tsw_comparator: the lion, mighty among animals, which does not turn back before anything;

verses.rationale: Flag girded loins animal and al-qum uncertainty.
verses.before: the strutting rooster, the male goat, and a king with an army around him.
verses.after: the strutting rooster, the male goat, and a king with his army beside him.
verses.tsw_comparator: the strutting rooster, the male goat, and a king with an army around him.

verses.before: If you have acted foolishly by exalting yourself, or if you have planned evil, put your hand over your mouth.
verses.after: If you have acted foolishly by exalting yourself, or if you have schemed—put your hand over your mouth!
verses.tsw_comparator: If you have acted foolishly by exalting yourself, or if you have planned evil, put your hand over your mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserve threefold pressing and nose/anger wordplay.
verses.before: For pressing milk produces curds, pressing the nose produces blood, and pressing anger produces conflict.
verses.after: For pressing milk produces curds, pressing a nose produces blood, and pressing anger produces a quarrel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For pressing milk produces curds, pressing the nose produces blood, and pressing anger produces conflict.

verses.rationale: Keep maternal royal instruction and oracle/Massa ambiguity.
verses.before: The words of King Lemuel, an oracle that his mother taught him:
verses.after: The words of King Lemuel. An oracle his mother taught him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of King Lemuel, an oracle that his mother taught him:

verses.before: What, my son? What, son of my womb? What, son of my vows?
verses.after: What, my son? What, son of my womb? What, son of my vows?
verses.tsw_comparator: What, my son? What, son of my womb? What, son of my vows?

verses.before: Do not give your strength to women, or your ways to people who destroy kings.
verses.after: Do not give your strength to women or your ways to what destroys kings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not give your strength to women, or your ways to those who destroy kings.

verses.rationale: Follow where read form rather than written or.
verses.before: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to desire strong drink,
verses.after: It is not for kings, Lemuel, not for kings to drink wine, nor for rulers to ask, “Where is strong drink?”
verses.tsw_comparator: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to desire strong drink,

verses.before: lest they drink and forget what is decreed and distort the rights of all the afflicted.
verses.after: They may drink and forget what is decreed and distort the rights of all the afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest they drink and forget what is decreed and distort the rights of all the afflicted.

verses.rationale: Keep stark contrasting instruction, not medical advice.
verses.before: Give strong drink to the one who is perishing and wine to those bitter in life.
verses.after: Give strong drink to one who is perishing and wine to those bitter in soul.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give strong drink to the one who is perishing and wine to those bitter in life.

verses.before: Let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their misery no more.
verses.after: Let him drink and forget his poverty and remember his misery no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their misery no more.

verses.rationale: Preserve difficult passing-away phrase; note destitute interpretation.
verses.before: Open your mouth for those without a voice, for the rights of everyone who are passing away.
verses.after: Open your mouth for those unable to speak, for the rights of all who are passing away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Open your mouth for those without a voice, for the rights of all who are passing away.

verses.rationale: Repeat speaking imperative and legal defense.
verses.before: Open your mouth; judge with righteousness; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verses.after: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the rights of the afflicted and needy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Open your mouth; judge with righteousness; defend the rights of the poor and needy.

verses.rationale: Retain chayil’s strength, not sexual virtue alone.
verses.before: A woman of strength— who can find? Her worth is far beyond jewels.
verses.after: A woman of strength—who can find her? Her worth is far beyond jewels.
verses.tsw_comparator: A woman of strength— who can find? Her worth is far beyond jewels.

verses.before: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will not lack gain.
verses.after: Her husband’s heart trusts her; he will lack no gain.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will not lack gain.

verses.before: She does him good and not harm all the days of her life.
verses.after: She does him good, not harm, all the days of her life.
verses.tsw_comparator: She does him good and not harm all the days of her life.

verses.before: She seeks wool and flax and works with willing hands.
verses.after: She seeks wool and flax and works with willing hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: She seeks wool and flax and works with willing hands.

verses.before: She is like merchant ships; she brings her food from far away.
verses.after: She is like a merchant’s ships, bringing her food from far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: She is like merchant ships; she brings her food from far away.

verses.rationale: Preserve provisions; note allotment/work assignment ambiguity.
verses.before: She rises while it is still night and gives food to her household and portions to her servants.
verses.after: She rises while it is still night, gives food to her household and an allotment to her young women.
verses.tsw_comparator: She rises while it is still night and gives food to her household and portions to her servants.

verses.rationale: Follow feminine plants read form; preserve economic agency.
verses.before: She considers a field and buys it; from the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.
verses.after: She considers a field and buys it; from the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.
verses.tsw_comparator: She considers a field and buys it; from the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily strength rather than mere resolve.
verses.before: She girds herself with strength and makes her arms strong.
verses.after: She girds her waist with strength and makes her arms strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: She girds herself with strength and makes her arms strong.

verses.rationale: Follow night read form; retain trade and lamp.
verses.before: She perceives that her merchandise is good; her lamp does not go out at night.
verses.after: She sees that her trading is profitable; her lamp does not go out at night.
verses.tsw_comparator: She perceives that her merchandise is good; her lamp does not go out at night.

verses.before: She reaches her hands to the distaff, and her palms hold the spindle.
verses.after: She reaches her hands to the distaff; her palms hold the spindle.
verses.tsw_comparator: She reaches her hands to the distaff, and her palms hold the spindle.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated hands connecting labor and generosity.
verses.before: She opens her palm to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
verses.after: She opens her palm to the afflicted and reaches out her hands to the needy.
verses.tsw_comparator: She opens her palm to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned scarlet rather than doubled garments.
verses.before: She does not fear snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet.
verses.after: She does not fear snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet.
verses.tsw_comparator: She does not fear snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet.

verses.rationale: Keep costly materials and her own use.
verses.before: She makes coverings for herself; fine linen and purple are her clothing.
verses.after: She makes coverings for herself; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
verses.tsw_comparator: She makes coverings for herself; fine linen and purple are her clothing.

verses.before: Her husband is known at the city gates when he sits with the elders of the land.
verses.after: Her husband is known at the gates, where he sits with the elders of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her husband is known at the city gates when he sits with the elders of the land.

verses.rationale: Render Canaanite by commercial sense; note literal term.
verses.before: She makes linen garments and sells them and supplies belts to the merchant.
verses.after: She makes linen garments and sells them; she supplies belts to the merchant.
verses.tsw_comparator: She makes linen garments and sells them and supplies belts to the merchant.

verses.before: Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the days to come.
verses.after: Strength and dignity are her clothing; she laughs at the day to come.
verses.tsw_comparator: Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the days to come.

verses.before: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the instruction of steadfast love is on her tongue.
verses.after: She opens her mouth with wisdom; instruction in faithful love is on her tongue.
verses.tsw_comparator: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the instruction of steadfast love is on her tongue.

verses.before: She watches carefully over the ways of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
verses.after: She watches over her household’s ways and does not eat the bread of idleness.
verses.tsw_comparator: She watches carefully over the ways of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.

verses.before: Her children rise and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praises her:
verses.after: Her children rise and call her happy; her husband rises and praises her:
verses.tsw_comparator: Her children rise and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praises her:

verses.before: “Many daughters have acted with strength, but you surpass them all.”
verses.after: “Many women have shown strength, but you surpass them all.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Many daughters have acted with strength, but you surpass them all.”

verses.rationale: Keep hevel image and fear-of-LORD conclusion.
verses.before: Charm is deceptive, and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
verses.after: Charm deceives, and beauty is a breath, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
verses.tsw_comparator: Charm is deceptive, and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.

verses.rationale: Retain her deserved earnings and public recognition.
verses.before: Give her from the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
verses.after: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her at the gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give her from the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
